Requirement text: Verify that input is decoded or unescaped into a canonical form only once, it is only decoded when encoded data in that form is expected, and that this is done before processing the input further, for example it is not performed after input validation or sanitization.
Evidence or reason: No decodeURI/decodeURIComponent/unescape/atob anywhere in server/ or client/src (grep of whole tree); Express decodes request paths and bodies exactly once in the body parsers (server/index.ts:23-24); SCORM package paths are normalised once at upload (server/routes.ts:4949-4954) and looked up by exact stored string (routes.ts:5093-5096). Residual: JSON.parse of relativePaths (routes.ts:1145) is a single parse of expected JSON.

Requirement text: Verify that the application performs output encoding and escaping either as a final step before being used by the interpreter for which it is intended or by the interpreter itself.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Print view escapes every stored value; every CSV export neutralises formula cells; download filenames are encoded (server/security.ts escapeHtml, csvSafe, contentDisposition). Tested by: tests/security/helpers.unit.ts, tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Encoding is applied at the point of use in most places, but the HTML print view, CSV exports and inline file downloads skip it, so stored content can alter the document (stored XSS in the print view, formula injection in exports).
Gap: Other places that build HTML or email text from stored data have not been walked through.
Fix: Add one shared escapeHtml helper and use it in the print view; prefix cells starting with = + - @ in every CSV export.

Requirement text: Verify that output encoding for an HTTP response, HTML document, or XML document is relevant for the context required, such as encoding the relevant characters for HTML elements, HTML attributes, HTML comments, CSS, or HTTP header fields, to avoid changing the message or document structure.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): The competence print view escapes every stored value; downloads use encoded filenames. Tested by: tests/security/helpers.unit.ts, tests/security/api.e2e.cjs (markup in a standard comes out as text). Original finding: The print view injects stored competence text straight into HTML, so anyone who can author standards can run script in the browser of every user who opens the print view; filename headers are inconsistent.

Requirement text: Verify that when dynamically building URLs, untrusted data is encoded according to its context (e.g., URL encoding or base64url encoding for query or path parameters). Ensure that only safe URL protocols are permitted (e.g., disallow javascript: or data:).
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Provider website, learning-content link, certificate link and any url field are refused unless http(s) or an in-app path (middleware in routes.ts, safeHttpUrl). Tested by: tests/security/helpers.unit.ts, tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: A stored javascript: or data: link in a provider website or learning-content link runs script when another user clicks it.
Gap: Links already stored before this change are not cleaned, and the pages that draw links do not re-check them.
Fix: Validate URL fields server-side to http/https only and apply the same check when rendering hrefs.

Requirement text: Verify that output encoding or escaping is used when dynamically building JavaScript content (including JSON), to avoid changing the message or document structure (to avoid JavaScript and JSON injection).
Evidence or reason: Server never builds JavaScript or inline script: no '<script' in server/ other than a comment (grep; routes.ts:5089); API output is res.json throughout; the single HTML shell comes from Vite/static index (server/vite.ts:48-62,71-84); client dangerouslySetInnerHTML only in the shadcn chart style tag with developer-defined config (client/src/components/ui/chart.tsx:80-98); no other innerHTML/document.write in client/src.

Requirement text: Verify that data selection or database queries (e.g., SQL, HQL, NoSQL, Cypher) use parameterized queries, ORMs, entity frameworks, or are otherwise protected from SQL Injection and other database injection attacks. This is also relevant when writing stored procedures.
Evidence or reason: All data access uses Drizzle builders or sql`` tagged templates whose ${} values become bound parameters; no sql.raw / sql.join / sql.identifier and no string-built queries (grep of server/ and shared/): routes.ts:6628-6631, 6754, 6820, 7249-7330; services/assessmentPlanning.ts:35-39; storage.ts:4815,4819 (search text passed as a parameter). Residual: ILIKE patterns do not escape % and _ (storage.ts:4815, services/auditLog.ts:196) which only affects matching, not injection. Hand-run DB tests (SQLi scan) still advisable.

Requirement text: Verify that the application protects against OS command injection and that operating system calls use parameterized OS queries or use contextual command line output encoding.
Evidence or reason: The only OS call is execSync in server/index.ts:106, interpolating parseInt(process.env.PORT) (a number) into a fixed shell string; no other child_process/exec/spawn use in server/, shared/ or client/src (grep). No user input reaches an OS call. Note: that command runs 'kill -9' on whoever holds the port, which should be removed for container hosting.

Requirement text: Verify that the application protects against LDAP injection vulnerabilities, or that specific security controls to prevent LDAP injection have been implemented.
Evidence or reason: No LDAP client or directory query in the code or package.json (grep ldap across server, shared, client/src, package.json). Sign-in is OIDC (server/replitAuth.ts). Re-check if the customer's identity provider integration is built on LDAP.

Requirement text: Verify that the application is protected against XPath injection attacks by using query parameterization or precompiled queries.
Evidence or reason: No XPath/XQuery evaluation anywhere (grep xpath). XML is only parsed with fast-xml-parser into an object tree (routes.ts:4966), which has no XPath query facility.

Requirement text: Verify that LaTeX processors are configured securely (such as not using the "--shell-escape" flag) and an allowlist of commands is used to prevent LaTeX injection attacks.
Evidence or reason: No LaTeX processor or PDF generation by shell-out (grep latex; no child_process use). Printable output is HTML printed by the browser (services/elearningCertificates.ts:273).

Requirement text: Verify that the application escapes special characters in regular expressions (typically using a backslash) to prevent them from being misinterpreted as metacharacters.
Evidence or reason: No new RegExp() built from any input in server/, shared/ or client/src (grep); all regexes are fixed literals (e.g. services/elearningCertificates.ts:39,241-242; routes.ts:4951). Search text goes to ILIKE as a parameter, not a regex.

Requirement text: Verify that all untrusted HTML input from WYSIWYG editors or similar is sanitized using a well-known and secure HTML sanitization library or framework feature.
Evidence or reason: No WYSIWYG/rich-text editor in the client (no editor libraries in package.json; no contentEditable in client/src) and the server never accepts or stores user HTML as markup; free text is rendered by React. Uploaded HTML via SCORM/evidence is a separate problem (see V1.3.4, V1.3.5).

Requirement text: Verify that the application avoids the use of eval() or other dynamic code execution features such as Spring Expression Language (SpEL). Where there is no alternative, any user input being included must be sanitized before being executed.
Evidence or reason: No eval, new Function, vm.*, or string-argument setTimeout in server/, shared/ or client/src (grep). No expression-language libraries in package.json.

Requirement text: Verify that data being passed to a potentially dangerous context is sanitized beforehand to enforce safety measures, such as only allowing characters which are safe for this context and trimming input which is too long.
Evidence or reason: Good: object keys sanitised to [A-Za-z0-9._-] and length-capped (server/services/objectStorage.ts:25-30); avatar and CV uploads check an allowlist of MIME types (routes.ts:1304, 1364); certificate logo checked from file bytes, 1 MB cap (services/elearningCertificates.ts:49-59); colour regex (elearningCertificates.ts:39); notification subjects stripped of line breaks and capped at 200 (services/notifications.ts:33-37). Missing: evidence, training-content, certificate and OPITO uploads accept any type and trust the client MIME (routes.ts:135-138, 165-176, 4907, 6402, 7568-7619, 9227-9247); no length caps on free-text fields (auto-generated Zod schemas in shared/schema.ts, only 10 .min/.max calls in the file).
Gap: Several dangerous contexts (file type, file names in headers, long free text) are guarded in some routes and not others.
Fix: Add a shared upload filter (type allowlist, magic-byte check) and length limits on text fields in the insert schemas.

Requirement text: Verify that user-supplied Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) scriptable content is validated or sanitized to contain only tags and attributes (such as draw graphics) that are safe for the application, e.g., do not contain scripts and foreignObject.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Evidence, CV and photo uploads are limited to listed types, checked against the first bytes, stored with a server-decided type, and always sent back as a download unless a PDF or picture, under a sandbox policy. Tested by: tests/security/helpers.unit.ts, tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: A candidate can upload an SVG or HTML file as evidence; when an assessor or admin opens it, the script runs in the Capera origin with that person's session.

Requirement text: Verify that the application sanitizes or disables user-supplied scriptable or expression template language content, such as Markdown, CSS or XSL stylesheets, BBCode, or similar.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): SCORM files now get their own page policy (no framing by other sites, no forms elsewhere). They still run with the viewer's session. Tested by: by reading the code. Original finding: SCORM content from anyone with training-content create permission executes with full access to the application origin and the viewer's session.
Gap: SCORM content from anyone who may upload it runs on Capera's own address. Needs a separate cookieless address (depends on the hosting decision) and tighter upload rights.
Fix: Serve SCORM and user files from a separate sandbox origin (cookieless subdomain) with a postMessage bridge for SCORM API calls; restrict upload permission to trusted roles meanwhile.

Requirement text: Verify that the application protects against Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks, by validating untrusted data against an allowlist of protocols, domains, paths and ports and sanitizing potentially dangerous characters before using the data to call another service.
Evidence or reason: The server makes no outbound request to any user-supplied URL: only fixed endpoints in services/emailService.ts:136,155 and vendor SDK calls (OpenAI/Anthropic) with fixed hosts; no fetch/axios/http.request elsewhere in server/ (grep). Stored URLs (provider website, content externalUrl, evidence fileUrl) are only ever rendered to the browser, and evidence/AI review reads objects by storage key via the object store client (services/aiCompetencyReview.ts:29-31). Re-check when the customer IdP/OIDC discovery and webhook/Teams integrations are added.

Requirement text: Verify that the application protects against template injection attacks by not allowing templates to be built based on untrusted input. Where there is no alternative, any untrusted input being included dynamically during template creation must be sanitized or strictly validated.
Evidence or reason: No server-side template engine (no ejs/pug/handlebars/nunjucks in package.json or code). HTML is built with fixed template literals and e-mail templates use a restricted placeholder replacer that cannot evaluate expressions (services/notifications.ts:15-51).

Requirement text: Verify that the application appropriately sanitizes untrusted input before use in Java Naming and Directory Interface (JNDI) queries and that JNDI is configured securely to prevent JNDI injection attacks.
Evidence or reason: Node.js application; no JNDI or Java in the stack (package.json, server/).

Requirement text: Verify that the application sanitizes content before it is sent to memcache to prevent injection attacks.
Evidence or reason: No memcached client; sessions live in Postgres (connect-pg-simple, server/replitAuth.ts:12) and in-process Maps only (replitAuth.ts closedCache, notifications 'forget' cache). Re-check if the company platform adds a cache.

Requirement text: Verify that format strings which might resolve in an unexpected or malicious way when used are sanitized before being processed.
Evidence or reason: No printf-style or user-controlled format strings. console.error calls use fixed format strings with values as separate arguments (e.g. server/routes.ts:6636, services/notifications.ts:251 interpolates e-mail address into a template literal, not a format string). Subject/body templates only substitute {{name}} tokens from an allowlist (services/notifications.ts:15-51,91-95).

Requirement text: Verify that the application sanitizes user input before passing to mail systems to protect against SMTP or IMAP injection.
Evidence or reason: Subjects have whitespace/CRLF collapsed and are capped (services/notifications.ts:33-37); bodies escaped (notifications.ts:39-51); all sends go through one function (emailService.ts:116-170) and nodemailer builds headers. But recipients are joined into a single to-string (emailService.ts:129) from users.email, which is never format-validated: create-user checks only presence (server/routes.ts:1785-1789), the user PATCH takes any value (routes.ts:1223-1244) including for a user's own email, and audience.emails is used as given (services/notifications.ts:241).
Gap: An e-mail address value containing commas or other address syntax could add recipients to notification mail; no e-mail format validation.
Fix: Validate e-mail format (single address, no commas/CRLF) at every write path and send one message per recipient.

Requirement text: Verify that the application uses memory-safe string, safer memory copy and pointer arithmetic to detect or prevent stack, buffer, or heap overflows.
Evidence or reason: Memory-safe managed runtime (TypeScript/Node.js); no native addons or manual buffers beyond Buffer APIs used for file handling. Node/V8 and npm native dependencies are patched via the platform base image.

Requirement text: Verify that sign, range, and input validation techniques are used to prevent integer overflows.
Evidence or reason: JavaScript numbers do not overflow in the C sense, and several services range-check integers (services/performance.ts:106-110,372,458; services/retention.ts:30-33). But request numbers on other routes are used unchecked: progressPercentage/timeSpentSeconds only typeof-checked (server/routes.ts:5276-5291), cost cast with String() (routes.ts:9136-9157), parseInt(req.body.order) without NaN check (routes.ts:4917, 5031), integer columns fed from the auto-generated schemas without ranges.
Gap: Out-of-range or NaN numbers from several routes reach the database (errors or nonsense values such as percentages over 100 or negative seconds).
Fix: Add range and integer checks (Zod .int().min().max()) on numeric inputs for progress, cost, order and capacity.

Requirement text: Verify that dynamically allocated memory and resources are released, and that references or pointers to freed memory are removed or set to null to prevent dangling pointers and use-after-free vulnerabilities.
Evidence or reason: Garbage-collected managed runtime; no manual memory management or native code in the application. Resource cleanup (pooled DB connections, streams) is handled by the libraries; stream error handlers exist at routes.ts:5101-5109, 5232-5240.

Requirement text: Verify that the application configures XML parsers to use a restrictive configuration and that unsafe features such as resolving external entities are disabled to prevent XML eXternal Entity (XXE) attacks.
Evidence or reason: XML is parsed in two places: SCORM imsmanifest.xml with fast-xml-parser (server/routes.ts:4968, default options, version pinned >=5.10.1 in package.json overrides) and DOCX/XLSX container XML inside mammoth/xlsx/pdf-parse libraries. fast-xml-parser does not resolve external entities or DTDs, so XXE is not possible with it, but no explicit processEntities:false is set and the other libraries' parser settings were not reviewed.
Gap: Safety rests on library defaults rather than an explicit restrictive configuration; third-party document parsers are unreviewed.
Fix: Set processEntities:false and a size cap on the manifest parser, and check mammoth/xlsx/pdf-parse versions against known advisories (see V1.5.2).

Requirement text: Verify that deserialization of untrusted data enforces safe input handling, such as using an allowlist of object types or restricting client-defined object types, to prevent deserialization attacks. Deserialization mechanisms that are explicitly defined as insecure must not be used with untrusted input.
Evidence or reason: No native deserialisation: only JSON.parse in guarded try/catch (server/routes.ts:1145-1147, 5141, services/aiTheming.ts:74,118) and sessions are JSON in Postgres. Weak spot: spreadsheets from admins are parsed with xlsx 0.18.5 (package.json; used at routes.ts:579, 3575, services/lifecycleImport.ts:115, trainingMatrixImport.ts:93), a version with published prototype-pollution and ReDoS advisories; also raw req.body is spread into database updates (routes.ts:1223, 8914-8926, 8502, 8594, 8667, 8771, 9324) so unexpected keys are written.
Gap: Old xlsx parser on uploaded files, and unfiltered request objects bound straight into updates.
Fix: Upgrade xlsx to the maintained build (or use exceljs) and bind request bodies through strict Zod schemas that reject unknown keys.

Requirement text: Verify that the application's documentation defines input validation rules for how to check the validity of data items against an expected structure. This could be common data formats such as credit card numbers, email addresses, telephone numbers, or it could be an internal data format.
Evidence or reason: No document defines validation rules for data items: replit.md only states 'Zod validation' in general terms (replit.md:31,43); FOLLOW_UPS.md:15 mentions one format question; security/ASVS_LEVEL2.md is a decision note, not rules. No data dictionary of formats (e-mail, vantage number, company number, dates).
Gap: There is no written definition of the expected structure of each input.
Fix: Write an input validation standard (per field: type, format, length, range) generated from the schemas.

Requirement text: Verify that the application's documentation defines how to validate the logical and contextual consistency of combined data items, such as checking that suburb and ZIP code match.
Evidence or reason: No documentation of cross-field consistency rules, although some exist in code (e.g. dates ordering services/performance.ts:119-121, 902-904; weightings add to 100, performance.ts:437).
Gap: Combined-field rules are implemented ad hoc and not documented.
Fix: Document cross-field rules per feature (dates, role and job role, manager chain, location and business unit) in the same standard.

Requirement text: Verify that expectations for business logic limits and validations are documented, including both per-user and globally across the application.
Evidence or reason: No document lists business limits (per user or global). Limits exist only as code constants: 10 MB / 200 MB upload caps (server/routes.ts:137,167,175), 500 MB uncompressed SCORM (routes.ts:5046), audit list cap 500 (services/auditLog.ts:201). No limit on AI calls, uploads per user or bookings.
Gap: Business limits are neither documented nor consistently set.
Fix: Document and then implement limits (upload quota, AI calls, booking capacity, bulk sizes) per user and global.

Requirement text: Verify that input is validated to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. This should either use positive validation against an allow list of values, patterns, and ranges, or be based on comparing the input to an expected structure and logical limits according to predefined rules. For L1, this can focus on input which is used to make specific business or security decisions. For L2 and up, this should apply to all input.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): User update, booking update, certificate routes and the print view now validate and allow-list fields. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Validation is positive in some modules but absent in a large number of routes, including ones that bind the whole request object into the database.
Gap: Most other routes still pass the request body through.
Fix: Validate every request body with a strict Zod schema (allowlisted fields, lengths, formats) via one shared middleware, starting with the routes listed.

Requirement text: Verify that the application is designed to enforce input validation at a trusted service layer. While client-side validation improves usability and should be encouraged, it must not be relied upon as a security control.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): User edit and booking edit use allow-lists by who is asking (self, administrator, booking owner); unknown fields are dropped. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Server-side validation exists, but several routes trust whatever fields the client sends, letting an ordinary user alter fields they should not control (own retention hold, own booking status/completion, object-storage keys).
Gap: Other update routes (providers, venues, courses, sessions, policy, appraisal and others) are not yet done.
Fix: Replace deny-lists with allowlisted Zod schemas per role on user PATCH and booking PUT, and reject unknown keys everywhere.

Requirement text: Verify that the application ensures that combinations of related data items are reasonable according to the pre-defined rules.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): A person can no longer change or create their own training record dates; the dates route is administrators only; assessors cannot assess or sign off themselves; a verifier cannot be the assessor or candidate. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Several related-field combinations are accepted without checks, notably a person extending their own certificate expiry date.
Gap: Reporting-line and other cross-field rules are not yet checked.
Fix: Add cross-field rules for training record dates, booking transitions, reporting lines and assessor != candidate.

Requirement text: Verify that the application will only process business logic flows for the same user in the expected sequential step order and without skipping steps.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Bookings: only administrators confirm, complete or re-price; owners can only cancel; confirming checks the seat. Verification needs allocation. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Assessment, verification, booking and training-request flows do not enforce step order, so steps can be skipped or repeated.
Gap: Assessment sign-off has no required previous state; training requests have no step check.
Fix: Add explicit status-transition checks (and DB conditions on the update) to assessment sign-off, verification, booking and request routes.

Requirement text: Verify that business logic limits are implemented per the application's documentation to avoid business logic flaws being exploited.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Seat capacity is now enforced (under a lock); assessor cannot assess themselves; verifier cannot verify their own assessment; AI and sign-in calls are limited per person or address. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Key business limits (course capacity, no self-assessment, one verifier per assessment, usage caps) are not enforced.
Gap: Other limits (upload quotas) are not set.
Fix: Implement and test the documented limits, starting with seat capacity, assessor != candidate, verifier != assessor and per-user upload/AI quotas.

Requirement text: Verify that transactions are being used at the business logic level such that either a business logic operation succeeds in its entirety or it is rolled back to the previous correct state.
Evidence or reason: Transactions are used in only five places (storage.ts:1196, 1350, 5654, 5674; services/retention.ts:92). Multi-step business operations run as separate statements: createVerification inserts then updates the assessment (storage.ts:5931-5941); fulfil request creates a booking, syncs the enrolment and then updates the request (routes.ts:9150-9165); sign-off writes history then overwrites the assessment (storage.ts:5589-5615); job role assignment, bulk imports and SCORM upload (routes.ts:5020-5083, with manual compensating clean-up at 5090-5110).
Gap: Most multi-step operations are not atomic, so a failure part-way leaves inconsistent compliance records.
Fix: Wrap each multi-write business operation (verification, sign-off, fulfilment, import apply, role assignment) in a db.transaction.

Requirement text: Verify that business logic level locking mechanisms are used to ensure that limited quantity resources (such as theater seats or delivery slots) cannot be double-booked by manipulating the application's logic.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Booking confirmation and new requests take a database lock per session so the last seat cannot be taken twice. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs (several requests at once). Original finding: A course session can be over-booked and a person double-booked by concurrent requests; capacity is not enforced at all.
Gap: Other multi-step changes (verification create, role-allocation changes) are not in a transaction.
Fix: Enforce capacity in a transaction with a row lock (or conditional UPDATE of seats_remaining) and add a unique (session_id, user_id) active-booking index.

Requirement text: Verify that anti-automation controls are in place to protect against excessive calls to application functions that could lead to data exfiltration, garbage-data creation, quota exhaustion, rate-limit breaches, denial-of-service, or overuse of costly resources.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): In-memory limits: sign-in 30 per 10 minutes per address; AI, translation and generation 60 per hour per person. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: A single user or script can drive unlimited AI calls, uploads, exports or searches, causing cost, denial of service or bulk data extraction.
Gap: The limit lives in one server process; behind several copies it moves to the shared store. No limits yet on uploads, exports and other costly calls.
Fix: Add per-user/IP rate limits (express-rate-limit with a shared store), per-user quotas on AI and upload endpoints, and pagination caps on list/export endpoints; add platform WAF limits.

Requirement text: Verify that security controls are in place to prevent browsers from rendering content or functionality in HTTP responses in an incorrect context (e.g., when an API, a user-uploaded file or other resource is requested directly). Possible controls could include: not serving the content unless HTTP request header fields (such as Sec-Fetch-\*) indicate it is the correct context, using the sandbox directive of the Content-Security-Policy header field or using the attachment disposition type in the Content-Disposition header field.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Uploaded files are served as a download under a neutral type unless PDF or picture; nosniff on every response; sandbox policy on downloads. Tested by: tests/security/helpers.unit.ts, tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: A candidate can upload an HTML file as 'evidence' (upload.array at routes.ts:7568 has no type check) and it is returned as text/html on the application's own origin when an assessor opens /api/assessment-evidence/:id/download in a new tab (VerifierDashboard.tsx:677), so the script runs with the assessor's session. Training content and SCORM files are served the same way, and the SCORM URL can be opened directly with no iframe sandbox at all.

Requirement text: Verify that content intended to be displayed as text, rather than rendered as HTML, is handled using safe rendering functions (such as createTextNode or textContent) to prevent unintended execution of content such as HTML or JavaScript.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Print view escapes stored text. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: The competence print view interpolates stored standard text (imported from Word/Excel documents) straight into HTML for any signed-in user, so markup in an imported standard executes in the viewer's session. The client side is sound.

Requirement text: Verify that cookies have the 'Secure' attribute set, and if the '\__Host-' prefix is not used for the cookie name, the '__Secure-' prefix must be used for the cookie name.
Evidence or reason: server/replitAuth.ts:52 (secure: true in production session cookie); cookie name is not set, so express-session uses its default connect.sid (server/replitAuth.ts:45-54); local-dev branch at server/replitAuth.ts:121 uses secure: false (LOCAL_DEV_AUTH only)
Gap: Secure is set, but the cookie name carries neither the __Host- nor the __Secure- prefix.
Fix: Set the session cookie name to a __Host- prefixed name (see V3.3.3).

Requirement text: Verify that each cookie's 'SameSite' attribute value is set according to the purpose of the cookie, to limit exposure to user interface redress attacks and browser-based request forgery attacks, commonly known as cross-site request forgery (CSRF).
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Session cookie is SameSite=Lax (server/replitAuth.ts). Tested by: by reading the code; confirm in the real sign-in flow on the deployment. Original finding: No SameSite attribute is set on the session cookie, so protection against cross-site requests depends on each browser's default (Lax-by-default is not applied by every browser, and Chrome allows cross-site top-level POST for 2 minutes after a no-SameSite cookie is set).

Requirement text: Verify that cookies have the '__Host-' prefix for the cookie name unless they are explicitly designed to be shared with other hosts.
Evidence or reason: server/replitAuth.ts:45-54 (no name option, so the default connect.sid is used)
Gap: The session cookie does not use the __Host- prefix and is not designed to be shared with other hosts.
Fix: Set name: '__Host-capera.sid' (requires Secure, Path=/, no Domain, which the current options already satisfy) and re-test sign-in behind the company proxy.

Requirement text: Verify that if the value of a cookie is not meant to be accessible to client-side scripts (such as a session token), the cookie must have the 'HttpOnly' attribute set and the same value (e. g. session token) must only be transferred to the client via the 'Set-Cookie' header field.
Evidence or reason: server/replitAuth.ts:51 (httpOnly: true); session id only travels in Set-Cookie (express-session); no access/refresh token or session id is returned in any JSON response (grep of server/ for access_token, refresh_token, sessionID outside replitAuth.ts finds none); client/src has no localStorage/sessionStorage use for tokens (only theme values in contexts/SectorThemeContext.tsx and ThemeContext.tsx)

Requirement text: Verify that a Strict-Transport-Security header field is included on all responses to enforce an HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) policy. A maximum age of at least 1 year must be defined, and for L2 and up, the policy must apply to all subdomains as well.
Evidence or reason: No Strict-Transport-Security set anywhere: grep of server/ for setHeader/helmet/Strict-Transport finds nothing relevant; package.json has no helmet dependency
Gap: The application never sends HSTS. The company ingress might add it, but nothing in the code or deployment files guarantees that.
Fix: Add helmet (or a small middleware) sending Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, and confirm with IT that the ingress does not strip it.

Requirement text: Verify that the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Access-Control-Allow-Origin header field is a fixed value by the application, or if the Origin HTTP request header field value is used, it is validated against an allowlist of trusted origins. When 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' needs to be used, verify that the response does not include any sensitive information.
Evidence or reason: No CORS middleware: package.json has no cors dependency and grep -i 'Access-Control' over server/ returns nothing, so no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is ever sent and the API is same-origin only; the client is served from the same origin (server/vite.ts:79-85)

Requirement text: Verify that HTTP responses include a Content-Security-Policy response header field which defines directives to ensure the browser only loads and executes trusted content or resources, in order to limit execution of malicious JavaScript. As a minimum, a global policy must be used which includes the directives object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' and defines either an allowlist or uses nonces or hashes. For an L3 application, a per-response policy with nonces or hashes must be defined.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): A strict content policy is sent in production (own scripts only, no framing, no plug-ins, forms to self); checked on the built app with no violations. SCORM files get a looser policy. Tested by: loaded the built app with the strict policy in the browser: no violations. Original finding: No CSP at all, so nothing limits script execution if any of the stored-content XSS paths in V3.2.1 or V3.2.2 is exploited; a third-party Replit script is loaded on every page in production.
Gap: Web fonts still come from Google; SCORM files need inline scripts. Fonts to be hosted by Capera.
Fix: Send a global CSP with default-src 'self', object-src 'none', base-uri 'none', frame-ancestors 'none' (and a per-route sandbox CSP for file and SCORM routes), and remove the replit-dev-banner script from client/index.html.

Requirement text: Verify that all HTTP responses contain an 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header field. This instructs browsers not to use content sniffing and MIME type guessing for the given response, and to require the response's Content-Type header field value to match the destination resource. For example, the response to a request for a style is only accepted if the response's Content-Type is 'text/css'. This also enables the use of the Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) functionality by the browser.
Evidence or reason: No X-Content-Type-Options header set anywhere in server/ (no helmet; express.static at server/vite.ts:79 sets none)
Gap: Responses are not marked nosniff; combined with user-controlled Content-Type on downloads this allows content to be interpreted differently from its declared type.
Fix: Add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff globally (helmet).

Requirement text: Verify that the application sets a referrer policy to prevent leakage of technically sensitive data to third-party services via the 'Referer' HTTP request header field. This can be done using the Referrer-Policy HTTP response header field or via HTML element attributes. Sensitive data could include path and query data in the URL, and for internal non-public applications also the hostname.
Evidence or reason: No Referrer-Policy header (server/) and no meta referrer or referrerpolicy attributes in client/index.html; external requests to fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com at client/index.html:8-11
Gap: No referrer policy is set, so full URLs (which can contain user and record ids) may be sent to the font host and to external training links.
Fix: Send Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or no-referrer) globally and self-host the fonts.

Requirement text: Verify that the web application uses the frame-ancestors directive of the Content-Security-Policy header field for every HTTP response to ensure that it cannot be embedded by default and that embedding of specific resources is allowed only when necessary. Note that the X-Frame-Options header field, although supported by browsers, is obsolete and may not be relied upon.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): frame-ancestors 'self' and X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN on every response. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Every page and response can be framed by any site, so a hostile page can overlay the app and trick a signed-in user into clicking (assessor approvals, certificate approval, user changes).

Requirement text: Verify that, if the application does not rely on the CORS preflight mechanism to prevent disallowed cross-origin requests to use sensitive functionality, these requests are validated to ensure they originate from the application itself. This may be done by using and validating anti-forgery tokens or requiring extra HTTP header fields that are not CORS-safelisted request-header fields. This is to defend against browser-based request forgery attacks, commonly known as cross-site request forgery (CSRF).
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Every change request (not GET) is refused if the browser says it came from another site (Sec-Fetch-Site or Origin); urlencoded bodies are no longer accepted; the session cookie is SameSite=Lax. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: State-changing routes (including POST /api/auth/impersonate, user, role, certificate and evidence routes) accept cross-site form posts: urlencoded and multipart bodies are parsed, authentication is a cookie with no SameSite attribute, and there is no token or header check.

Requirement text: Verify that, if the application relies on the CORS preflight mechanism to prevent disallowed cross-origin use of sensitive functionality, it is not possible to call the functionality with a request which does not trigger a CORS-preflight request. This may require checking the values of the 'Origin' and 'Content-Type' request header fields or using an extra header field that is not a CORS-safelisted header-field.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): As V3.5.1: protection does not rely on preflight. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: The API does not rely on preflight for protection yet can still be called without preflight (urlencoded form posts and multipart uploads), so the requirement is not satisfied; same root cause as V3.5.1.

Requirement text: Verify that HTTP requests to sensitive functionality use appropriate HTTP methods such as POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE, and not methods defined by the HTTP specification as "safe" such as HEAD, OPTIONS, or GET. Alternatively, strict validation of the Sec-Fetch-* request header fields can be used to ensure that the request did not originate from an inappropriate cross-origin call, a navigation request, or a resource load (such as an image source) where this is not expected.
Evidence or reason: Mutating routes use POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE (server/routes.ts, performanceRoutes.ts, certificateRoutes.ts etc.); a scripted scan of every app.get handler in server/*.ts for storage/db write calls found no state change in GET handlers; counter-example: server/replitAuth.ts:188-197 GET /api/logout ends the session (and GET /api/login:174 starts an authorisation flow)
Gap: Almost all GET routes are read-only, but logout is a GET, so any page can log a user out with an image tag; sign-in is also a GET.
Fix: Make logout a POST (client/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:67 then calls it with fetch).

Requirement text: Verify that separate applications are hosted on different hostnames to leverage the restrictions provided by same-origin policy, including how documents or scripts loaded by one origin can interact with resources from another origin and hostname-based restrictions on cookies.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): As V1.3.5: untrusted package content still shares the application's address. Tested by: by reading the code. Original finding: Untrusted content (SCORM packages, evidence, training documents) shares the origin and cookies of the authenticated application, so same-origin protections do not separate them; a SCORM package's script can call every API as the viewer and reach window.parent.
Gap: Separate cookieless address for SCORM and downloads.
Fix: Serve SCORM packages and user-supplied files from a separate hostname (cookieless, via short-lived signed URLs) and drop allow-same-origin from the iframe sandbox with a postMessage-based SCORM bridge.

Requirement text: Verify that messages received by the postMessage interface are discarded if the origin of the message is not trusted, or if the syntax of the message is invalid.
Evidence or reason: grep of client/src for postMessage and addEventListener('message') finds nothing; the SCORM bridge in client/src/components/ScormPlayer.tsx:14-120 uses direct window.API objects, not postMessage. Note: if SCORM is later moved to a separate origin a postMessage bridge will be needed and this requirement will then apply

Requirement text: Verify that the application only uses client-side technologies which are still supported and considered secure. Examples of technologies which do not meet this requirement include NSAPI plugins, Flash, Shockwave, ActiveX, Silverlight, NACL, or client-side Java applets.
Evidence or reason: Client is React/TypeScript/Vite only (package.json; client/src); grep of client/src for <object, <embed, applet, ActiveX, swfobject finds nothing; the only embedded content is the sandboxed iframes at client/src/components/ScormPlayer.tsx:141 and NotificationSettings.tsx:333. SCORM packages themselves are third-party content and routes.ts:4934-4940 maps .swf to a MIME type, but nothing executes plugins

Requirement text: Verify that the application will only automatically redirect the user to a different hostname or domain (which is not controlled by the application) where the destination appears on an allowlist.
Evidence or reason: The only server redirects are res.redirect('/') in server/replitAuth.ts:132-134 and the identity provider end-session URL built from OIDC discovery at server/replitAuth.ts:190-195 (grep for res.redirect in server/ finds no other); the client assigns window.location.href only to fixed paths (client/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:63,67; Landing.tsx:71); external links (externalUrl, provider.website) open only on user click with rel=noopener. Re-check when the customer identity provider replaces replitAuth.ts

Requirement text: Verify that every HTTP response with a message body contains a Content-Type header field that matches the actual content of the response, including the charset parameter to specify safe character encoding (e.g., UTF-8, ISO-8859-1) according to IANA Media Types, such as "text/", "/+xml" and "/xml".
Evidence or reason: res.json always sends application/json; charset=utf-8 (Express); server/auditRoutes.ts:30, certificateRoutes.ts:47,71 set charset. Counter-examples without charset or without any Content-Type: server/routes.ts:3362 (text/html), 5099 (SCORM files, text/html and application/javascript from the lookup at 4930-4936), 5226 (content only set if mimeType exists), 8342 and 9204 (text/csv), 1338 (avatar), 7399
Gap: Several routes send text types without a charset, and the training-content download sends no Content-Type at all when the stored mime type is empty.
Fix: Add charset=utf-8 to every text/* type and set a default Content-Type of application/octet-stream when none is stored.

Requirement text: Verify that only user-facing endpoints (intended for manual web-browser access) automatically redirect from HTTP to HTTPS, while other services or endpoints do not implement transparent redirects. This is to avoid a situation where a client is erroneously sending unencrypted HTTP requests, but since the requests are being automatically redirected to HTTPS, the leakage of sensitive data goes undiscovered.
Evidence or reason: The application has no HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect of its own (grep of server/ finds none; session cookie is Secure at server/replitAuth.ts:52). The platform must terminate TLS and either refuse plain HTTP for /api or redirect only for the browser-facing pages, and set X-Forwarded-Proto so express-session issues Secure cookies (trust proxy is 1 at replitAuth.ts:102)

Requirement text: Verify that any HTTP header field used by the application and set by an intermediary layer, such as a load balancer, a web proxy, or a backend-for-frontend service, cannot be overridden by the end-user. Example headers might include X-Real-IP, X-Forwarded-*, or X-User-ID.
Evidence or reason: server/replitAuth.ts:102 (trust proxy 1, so req.ip takes the proxy-added address); counter-example: server/services/auditLog.ts:176 records the first value of the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header as the audit log IP, which an end user can set to any value; req.hostname is used to choose the OIDC strategy at replitAuth.ts:175,182 and for the post-logout redirect at 193
Gap: The audit log trusts the first X-Forwarded-For entry, so a user can forge the IP address recorded against their actions; the platform must also overwrite (not append to) forwarding headers and the proxy count must match trust proxy 1.
Fix: Use req.ip only (remove the header read at auditLog.ts:176), set trust proxy to the real number of hops, and have the ingress strip incoming X-Forwarded-* and X-User-* headers.

Requirement text: Verify that all application components (including load balancers, firewalls, and application servers) determine boundaries of incoming HTTP messages using the appropriate mechanism for the HTTP version to prevent HTTP request smuggling. In HTTP/1.x, if a Transfer-Encoding header field is present, the Content-Length header must be ignored per RFC 2616. When using HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, if a Content-Length header field is present, the receiver must ensure that it is consistent with the length of the DATA frames.
Evidence or reason: The app uses Node's built-in HTTP server behind Express (server/index.ts); request framing is done by the Node parser and the company's load balancer. The platform must use a current Node.js and a proxy that normalises Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length (HTTP/1.1 desync tests belong in the penetration test)

Requirement text: Verify that a query allowlist, depth limiting, amount limiting, or query cost analysis is used to prevent GraphQL or data layer expression Denial of Service (DoS) as a result of expensive, nested queries.
Evidence or reason: No GraphQL: grep for graphql/apollo across server/, shared/, client/src and package.json returns nothing; the API is REST over Express

Requirement text: Verify that GraphQL introspection queries are disabled in the production environment unless the GraphQL API is meant to be used by other parties.
Evidence or reason: No GraphQL: grep for graphql/apollo across server/, shared/, client/src and package.json returns nothing; the API is REST over Express

Requirement text: Verify that WebSocket over TLS (WSS) is used for all WebSocket connections.
Evidence or reason: No WebSocket server or client feature: grep for WebSocketServer, socket.io, the http upgrade event and EventSource in server/ and client/src finds nothing; the ws package is used only as the database driver transport in server/db.ts:5,12 and Vite hot reload exists only in development (server/vite.ts:26)

Requirement text: Verify that, during the initial HTTP WebSocket handshake, the Origin header field is checked against a list of origins allowed for the application.
Evidence or reason: No WebSocket server or client feature: grep for WebSocketServer, socket.io, the http upgrade event and EventSource in server/ and client/src finds nothing; the ws package is used only as the database driver transport in server/db.ts:5,12 and Vite hot reload exists only in development (server/vite.ts:26)

Requirement text: Verify that, if the application's standard session management cannot be used, dedicated tokens are being used for this, which comply with the relevant Session Management security requirements.
Evidence or reason: No WebSocket server or client feature: grep for WebSocketServer, socket.io, the http upgrade event and EventSource in server/ and client/src finds nothing; the ws package is used only as the database driver transport in server/db.ts:5,12 and Vite hot reload exists only in development (server/vite.ts:26)

Requirement text: Verify that dedicated WebSocket session management tokens are initially obtained or validated through the previously authenticated HTTPS session when transitioning an existing HTTPS session to a WebSocket channel.
Evidence or reason: No WebSocket server or client feature: grep for WebSocketServer, socket.io, the http upgrade event and EventSource in server/ and client/src finds nothing; the ws package is used only as the database driver transport in server/db.ts:5,12 and Vite hot reload exists only in development (server/vite.ts:26)

Requirement text: Verify that the documentation defines the permitted file types, expected file extensions, and maximum size (including unpacked size) for each upload feature. Additionally, ensure that the documentation specifies how files are made safe for end-users to download and process, such as how the application behaves when a malicious file is detected.
Evidence or reason: No file-handling documentation found: security/ contains only ASVS_LEVEL2.md and the asvs folder; replit.md and FOLLOW_UPS.md do not list permitted types, extensions, sizes or malicious-file handling per upload feature (limits exist only in code: server/routes.ts:135-137, 165-168, 173-176, certificateRoutes.ts:32)
Gap: There is no document listing, for each of the ten upload features (avatar, CV, evidence, training content, SCORM, certificates, OPITO documents, draft-standard documents, imports, logo), the allowed types, extensions, size, unpacked size and what happens to a malicious file.
Fix: Write a one-page upload matrix in security/ and keep it in step with the code.

Requirement text: Verify that the application will only accept files of a size which it can process without causing a loss of performance or a denial of service attack.
Evidence or reason: Size limits exist: server/routes.ts:135-138 (10 MB general), 165-168 (200 MB streamed), 173-176 (200 MB SCORM, held fully in memory), certificateRoutes.ts:32 (1.5 MB, files:1); express.json default 100 KB limit (server/index.ts:23). Counter-examples: no files/fields/parts limit on upload.array('files') at routes.ts:1136, 2598, 7568, so one request can carry unlimited 10 MB parts held in memory; SCORM and docx/xlsx importers buffer whole files with no concurrency limit and no rate limiting (no express-rate-limit in package.json)
Gap: Per-file size is capped but the number of files per request is not, and large in-memory uploads (200 MB SCORM) with no concurrency or rate control let one signed-in user (a candidate can use the evidence route) exhaust memory and take the service down for everyone.
Fix: Add files and fields limits to every multer instance, stream the SCORM zip to disk instead of memory, and add per-user rate limits on upload routes.

Requirement text: Verify that when the application accepts a file, either on its own or within an archive such as a zip file, it checks if the file extension matches an expected file extension and validates that the contents correspond to the type represented by the extension. This includes, but is not limited to, checking the initial 'magic bytes', performing image re-writing, and using specialized libraries for file content validation. For L1, this can focus just on files which are used to make specific business or security decisions. For L2 and up, this must apply to all files being accepted.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Evidence, CV and photo uploads check extension and file content; the stored type is decided by the server. Tested by: tests/security/helpers.unit.ts, tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: File type is mostly trusted from the browser-supplied header or filename and contents are never checked against it (a .pdf can be HTML), which also feeds the inline-serving problem in V3.2.1.
Gap: Spreadsheet/Word imports and learning content upload still trust the browser's type.
Fix: Add an allowlist of extensions per upload feature plus magic-byte validation (for example the file-type library, docx/xlsx zip structure checks) and store a server-determined content type.

Requirement text: Verify that the application checks compressed files (e.g., zip, gz, docx, odt) against maximum allowed uncompressed size and against maximum number of files before uncompressing the file.
Evidence or reason: server/routes.ts:5042-5063 SCORM: total uncompressed cap of 500 MB, checked after each entry is decompressed; counter-examples: no cap on the number of entries or on any single entry before decompression (JSZip.loadAsync at 5002 and entry.async at 5053); server/services/competenceCriteriaImport.ts:28-33 reads word/document.xml of an uploaded docx fully into memory with no size or entry-count check; XLSX.read on uploaded workbooks at routes.ts:579 and 3575 with no limits
Gap: The SCORM cap is applied only after each file has been expanded in memory, there is no limit on number of files, and docx/xlsx imports do not check expanded size at all, so a small crafted archive can exhaust memory.
Fix: Read the zip central directory first (JSZip entry _data.uncompressedSize) and reject on total size or entry count before extracting; apply the same pre-check to docx and xlsx imports.

Requirement text: Verify that files uploaded or generated by untrusted input and stored in a public folder, are not executed as server-side program code when accessed directly with an HTTP request.
Evidence or reason: Uploaded files are never written to a web-served folder: they go to object storage via buildObjectKey/uploadObject (server/services/objectStorage.ts:25-36, routes.ts:146-153) or the database (certificate logo); the only static folder is the built client, express.static(distPath) at server/vite.ts:71-79; Node does not execute uploaded files by path. (Client-side execution of served files is covered under V3.2.1.)

Requirement text: Verify that when the application creates file paths for file operations, instead of user-submitted filenames, it uses internally generated or trusted data, or if user-submitted filenames or file metadata must be used, strict validation and sanitization must be applied. This is to protect against path traversal, local or remote file inclusion (LFI, RFI), and server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks.
Evidence or reason: server/services/objectStorage.ts:21-31 builds every object key from a random UUID plus a character-whitelisted, length-limited name; every download takes the key from a database record, not from the request (routes.ts:1340, 1398, 5101, 5228, 6447, 7398, 9263); SCORM entries are rejected for '..' or '.' segments and stored under generated keys (routes.ts:4941-4945, 5057); SCORM serving is a database lookup of the requested path (storage.getScormPackageFile at routes.ts:5094) so no file path is built from the URL; no outbound fetch of user-supplied URLs exists (only fixed e-mail API hosts at server/services/emailService.ts:136,155)

Requirement text: Verify that the application validates or ignores user-submitted filenames, including in a JSON, JSONP, or URL parameter and specifies a filename in the Content-Disposition header field in the response.
Evidence or reason: Stored original names are used and every download except avatar and SCORM sets a filename in Content-Disposition (routes.ts:5227, 6448, 7400, 9265, 1396); counter-examples: routes.ts:9265 and 1396 interpolate the raw original filename in quotes (the CV route only strips double quotes; OPITO does not), so a quote or a non-Latin-1 character in a name breaks the header or makes Node throw; avatar (1338) and SCORM files (5099) set no Content-Disposition
Gap: Filenames are not validated before storage or output; names with quotes or non-Latin-1 characters can inject header parameters or cause a 500 on download.
Fix: Sanitise the name on upload and emit Content-Disposition through one helper that builds both filename and the RFC 6266 filename* form from a cleaned value.

Requirement text: Verify that file names served (e.g., in HTTP response header fields or email attachments) are encoded or sanitized (e.g., following RFC 6266) to preserve document structure and prevent injection attacks.
Evidence or reason: routes.ts:5227, 6448, 7400 wrap the name in encodeURIComponent (safe from injection, but not RFC 6266 form, so non-ASCII names display percent-encoded); routes.ts:9265 (OPITO) and 1396 (CV) use the raw name with at most quote stripping; server-generated CSV names are safe (routes.ts:5417, 8343, 9205; auditRoutes.ts:31)
Gap: Encoding is inconsistent: two routes put the raw uploaded name in the header and the others use a non-standard encoding.
Fix: Use one RFC 6266 helper (filename plus filename*) for all downloads.

Requirement text: Verify that files obtained from untrusted sources are scanned by antivirus scanners to prevent serving of known malicious content.
Evidence or reason: No antivirus or content scanning anywhere: grep of server/ and package.json for clam, antivirus, virus, scan returns nothing; files from candidates and external parties (evidence at routes.ts:7568, CVs 1355, certificates 6402, SCORM 4975) are stored and served to assessors and administrators unscanned
Gap: Uploaded files are never scanned, so known malware can be uploaded by one user and opened by an assessor or administrator. The company platform may scan its object storage, but the application has no hook or confirmation for it.
Fix: Scan each upload (ClamAV via clamd or the company's scanning service) before the record is created and quarantine on detection, or get IT to confirm scan-on-write on the storage bucket.

Requirement text: Verify that application documentation defines how controls such as rate limiting, anti-automation, and adaptive response, are used to defend against attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force. The documentation must make clear how these controls are configured and prevent malicious account lockout.
Evidence or reason: security/ASVS_LEVEL2.md and replit.md contain no statement of rate limiting, anti-automation or lockout design; package.json has no rate-limit package and server/index.ts:23-30 registers none.
Gap: Nothing documents how credential stuffing and brute force are countered or how malicious lockout is avoided. The application has no password endpoint, so the controls are the identity provider's, but that division is not written down, and the application itself has no throttling on /api/login or /api/callback.
Fix: Write a short authentication security note stating that the identity provider owns lockout and anti-automation (named settings, e.g. Entra smart lockout thresholds and Conditional Access) and that the app has no credential endpoint; add a basic rate limit on /api/login and /api/callback.

Requirement text: Verify that a list of context-specific words is documented in order to prevent their use in passwords. The list could include permutations of organization names, product names, system identifiers, project codenames, department or role names, and similar.
Evidence or reason: No document or configuration lists context-specific words (Capera, the customer name, product and system names); grep of security/ and replit.md finds none.
Gap: No list of organisation, product and system words to ban from passwords exists.
Fix: Document the list and load it into the identity provider's custom banned password list.

Requirement text: Verify that, if the application includes multiple authentication pathways, these are all documented together with the security controls and authentication strength which must be consistently enforced across them.
Evidence or reason: Pathways present in code: OIDC login (server/replitAuth.ts:157-186), local-dev auto sign-in (server/replitAuth.ts:104-136), administrator impersonation (server/routes.ts:403-433), refresh-token renewal (server/replitAuth.ts:229-243). Only code comments describe the dev bypass (server/replitAuth.ts:16-19); no document lists the pathways together with the strength each must enforce. Unused passport-local dependency at package.json:78.
Gap: The authentication pathways are not documented together with the controls and strength required on each.
Fix: Document the four pathways, who may use each and the required strength (MFA at the provider, no dev bypass in production, step-up for impersonation), and remove the unused passport-local dependency.

Requirement text: Verify that user set passwords are at least 8 characters in length although a minimum of 15 characters is strongly recommended.
Evidence or reason: The application stores and verifies no passwords: no bcrypt/argon2/scrypt/passport-local use anywhere in server/, shared/ or client/src (no LocalStrategy matches); sign-in is OIDC only (server/replitAuth.ts:157-186).

Requirement text: Verify that users can change their password.
Evidence or reason: No change-password feature in the app (no password route or field in server/routes.ts or client/src). Identity provider must offer self-service password change (e.g. Entra My Account / SSPR) or the company must use passwordless sign-in.

Requirement text: Verify that password change functionality requires the user's current and new password.
Evidence or reason: No password change in the app. The provider's change flow must require current and new password (Entra does for signed-in change; SSPR reset is a separate flow requiring MFA proof).

Requirement text: Verify that passwords submitted during account registration or password change are checked against an available set of, at least, the top 3000 passwords which match the application's password policy, e.g. minimum length.
Evidence or reason: No password registration in the app. Provider must enforce a banned-password check of at least the top 3000 (Entra Password Protection global banned list, enabled and in enforced mode).

Requirement text: Verify that passwords of any composition can be used, without rules limiting the type of characters permitted. There must be no requirement for a minimum number of upper or lower case characters, numbers, or special characters.
Evidence or reason: No password rules in the app. Caveat: Entra cloud accounts enforce a fixed 3-of-4 character-class composition rule that cannot be switched off, which conflicts with this requirement; satisfy by passwordless/FIDO2/Authenticator sign-in or record an accepted deviation with IT.

Requirement text: Verify that password input fields use type=password to mask the entry. Applications may allow the user to temporarily view the entire masked password, or the last typed character of the password.
Evidence or reason: No password input field exists in client/src (no type=password; sign-in is a redirect, client/src/pages/Landing.tsx:71). The provider's sign-in page must mask entry.

Requirement text: Verify that "paste" functionality, browser password helpers, and external password managers are permitted.
Evidence or reason: No password field in the app; paste and password managers are a property of the provider's sign-in page, which must not block them.

Requirement text: Verify that the application verifies the user's password exactly as received from the user, without any modifications such as truncation or case transformation.
Evidence or reason: The app never receives or verifies a password (no password handling in server/). Provider verifies as received.

Requirement text: Verify that passwords of at least 64 characters are permitted.
Evidence or reason: No password handling in the app. Provider must accept at least 64 characters (Entra accepts up to 256).

Requirement text: Verify that a user's password stays valid until it is discovered to be compromised or the user rotates it. The application must not require periodic credential rotation.
Evidence or reason: No password lifetime logic in the app. Provider must not force periodic rotation (Entra: set passwords not to expire, rotate only on compromise).

Requirement text: Verify that the documented list of context specific words is used to prevent easy to guess passwords being created.
Evidence or reason: No password creation in the app. Provider's custom banned password list must be loaded with the documented context words (see V6.1.2, which is not yet documented).

Requirement text: Verify that passwords submitted during account registration or password changes are checked against a set of breached passwords.
Evidence or reason: No password creation in the app. Provider must check against breached passwords (Entra Password Protection global list; Identity Protection leaked-credential detection if licensed).

Requirement text: Verify that controls to prevent attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force are implemented according to the application's security documentation.
Evidence or reason: No credential-verifying endpoint in the app (no password or OTP check in server/; /api/login only redirects to the provider, server/replitAuth.ts:174-179). Provider must provide smart lockout, Conditional Access, risk-based sign-in policy and block legacy authentication. The app has no rate limiter of its own (none in package.json).

Requirement text: Verify that default user accounts (e.g., "root", "admin", or "sa") are not present in the application or are disabled.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): The server refuses to start if LOCAL_DEV_AUTH is set in production. Tested by: run: refused with NODE_ENV=production. Original finding: A well-known administrator-level account is created whenever LOCAL_DEV_AUTH=true, and nothing stops that being set in production, which would sign every visitor in as a developer with no credential check.

Requirement text: Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms, must be used in order to access the application. For L3, one of the factors must be a hardware-based authentication mechanism which provides compromise and impersonation resistance against phishing attacks while verifying the intent to authenticate by requiring a user-initiated action (such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key or a mobile phone). Relaxing any of the considerations in this requirement requires a fully documented rationale and a comprehensive set of mitigating controls.
Evidence or reason: The app delegates all authentication (server/replitAuth.ts:157-186) and does not read acr/amr claims (grep finds none in server/), so MFA cannot be confirmed by the app. Provider must enforce MFA for this application via a Conditional Access policy (phishing-resistant for administrators), set 'assignment required' so only assigned users can sign in, and use a single-tenant issuer. Note the app auto-creates any signing-in subject as a candidate (server/replitAuth.ts:82-96).

Requirement text: Verify that, if the application includes multiple authentication pathways, there are no undocumented pathways and that security controls and authentication strength are enforced consistently.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): One gate on all of /api (token in date, account not closed, fail closed); only sign-in, callback, logout, login-refused and health are open. Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: A person whose account has been closed (leaver) or whose provider token has expired can keep using the 79 role-only routes, including assessment and evidence routes, for up to the 7-day session. The dev bypass and impersonation are additional unconstrained pathways.

Requirement text: Verify that system generated initial passwords or activation codes are securely randomly generated, follow the existing password policy, and expire after a short period of time or after they are initially used. These initial secrets must not be permitted to become the long term password.
Evidence or reason: The application generates no initial passwords or activation codes: users are created by import or by first OIDC sign-in with no credential (no password column in shared/schema.ts, no invite-code logic in server/). Any initial secret or Temporary Access Pass is the identity provider's.

Requirement text: Verify that password hints or knowledge-based authentication (so-called "secret questions") are not present.
Evidence or reason: No hints or secret questions in the app (grep of client/src and server/ finds none). Provider must have security-question reset methods disabled (Entra SSPR: use Authenticator/phone/email, not questions).

Requirement text: Verify that a secure process for resetting a forgotten password is implemented, that does not bypass any enabled multi-factor authentication mechanisms.
Evidence or reason: No password reset in the app. Provider's reset must require MFA and not bypass enabled factors (Entra SSPR with two methods and combined registration).

Requirement text: Verify that if a multi-factor authentication factor is lost, evidence of identity proofing is performed at the same level as during enrollment.
Evidence or reason: No factor management in the app. Company helpdesk/provider process must identity-proof at enrolment level when a factor is lost (e.g. Temporary Access Pass issued after verified identity check).

Requirement text: Verify that lookup secrets, out-of-band authentication requests or codes, and time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs) are only successfully usable once.
Evidence or reason: The app has no lookup secrets, out-of-band codes or TOTP (no otp/totp logic in server/; client/src/components/ui/input-otp.tsx is an unused UI component with no importers). MFA is the provider's.

Requirement text: Verify that, when being stored in the application's backend, lookup secrets with less than 112 bits of entropy (19 random alphanumeric characters or 34 random digits) are hashed with an approved password storage hashing algorithm that incorporates a 32-bit random salt. A standard hash function can be used if the secret has 112 bits of entropy or more.
Evidence or reason: The application stores no lookup secrets, OTP codes or TOTP seeds (no such tables in shared/schema.ts, no code in server/).

Requirement text: Verify that lookup secrets, out-of-band authentication code, and time-based one-time password seeds, are generated using a Cryptographically Secure Pseudorandom Number Generator (CSPRNG) to avoid predictable values.
Evidence or reason: The app generates no MFA secrets. Provider must use CSPRNG-generated codes and seeds (Entra Authenticator does).

Requirement text: Verify that lookup secrets and out-of-band authentication codes have a minimum of 20 bits of entropy (typically 4 random alphanumeric characters or 6 random digits is sufficient).
Evidence or reason: The app issues no codes (certificate numbers via crypto randomInt at server/services/elearningCertificates.ts:76 are not authentication codes). Provider's codes meet the 20-bit minimum.

Requirement text: Verify that out-of-band authentication requests, codes, or tokens, as well as time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs) have a defined lifetime. Out of band requests must have a maximum lifetime of 10 minutes and for TOTP a maximum lifetime of 30 seconds.
Evidence or reason: The app issues no out-of-band codes or TOTP. Provider lifetimes (Authenticator 30 s TOTP, OOB under 10 minutes) apply.

Requirement text: Verify that authentication mechanisms using the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) to deliver One-time Passwords (OTPs) via phone or SMS are offered only when the phone number has previously been validated, alternate stronger methods (such as Time based One-time Passwords) are also offered, and the service provides information on their security risks to users. For L3 applications, phone and SMS must not be available as options.
Evidence or reason: The app offers no PSTN OTP. Provider must disable SMS/voice authentication methods or offer them only with validated numbers alongside stronger methods (Authenticator, FIDO2).

Requirement text: Verify that out-of-band authentication requests, codes, or tokens are bound to the original authentication request for which they were generated and are not usable for a previous or subsequent one.
Evidence or reason: The app has no out-of-band authentication of its own. OIDC authorization codes are bound to the request by PKCE S256 in node_modules/openid-client/build/passport.js (code_challenge, stateData in session), and verified at callback, but the out-of-band factors are the provider's.

Requirement text: Verify that a code based out-of-band authentication mechanism is protected against brute force attacks by using rate limiting. Consider also using a code with at least 64 bits of entropy.
Evidence or reason: The app has no code-based out-of-band mechanism. Provider must rate-limit code entry (Entra smart lockout / MFA throttling).

Requirement text: Verify that, if the application supports multiple identity providers (IdPs), the user's identity cannot be spoofed via another supported identity provider (eg. by using the same user identifier). The standard mitigation would be for the application to register and identify the user using a combination of the IdP ID (serving as a namespace) and the user's ID in the IdP.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): A first sign-in is matched to an administrator-created account by email only if the account has no identity yet, and (when the provider sends the flag, or REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFIED=true) the email is verified; an account already tied to one identity is never re-keyed; roles are never taken from the provider. Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: Anyone who can present a token whose email claim equals an existing account's email (for example Entra, where email is mutable and unverified) takes over that account, including administrators, with its history. Migration from Replit to the company provider will depend on exactly this email re-keying.
Gap: Identity is still (subject) alone, not (issuer, tenant, subject); the company identity provider needs to be settled.
Fix: Store and look up identity as (issuer, tenant id, stable object id); stop auto-linking by email except through an admin-confirmed one-off mapping; require email_verified where used; ignore the role claim; strip email from non-admin self-updates.

Requirement text: Verify that the presence and integrity of digital signatures on authentication assertions (for example on JWTs or SAML assertions) are always validated, rejecting any assertions that are unsigned or have invalid signatures.
Evidence or reason: The ID token comes from the token endpoint via openid-client 6.8.0 (server/replitAuth.ts:1,142,159-167), whose oauth4webapi validateJwt rejects unsigned tokens and verifies the signature against keys from the issuer's jwks_uri: node_modules/oauth4webapi/build/index.js:1240 (id_token validation), 1696-1735 (validateJwt, alg check, crit rejected), 1060-1090 (key selection from as.jwks_uri). The app accepts no assertions from clients (no Authorization/bearer parsing in server/). Not exercised by a test.

Requirement text: Verify that SAML assertions are uniquely processed and used only once within the validity period to prevent replay attacks.
Evidence or reason: No SAML in the application; sign-in is OIDC authorization-code with PKCE only (server/replitAuth.ts:1,6; no saml dependency in package.json).

Requirement text: Verify that, if an application uses a separate Identity Provider (IdP) and expects specific authentication strength, methods, or recentness for specific functions, the application verifies this using the information returned by the IdP. For example, if OIDC is used, this might be achieved by validating ID Token claims such as 'acr', 'amr', and 'auth_time' (if present). If the IdP does not provide this information, the application must have a documented fallback approach that assumes that the minimum strength authentication mechanism was used (for example, single-factor authentication using username and password).
Evidence or reason: The app never inspects acr, amr or auth_time (grep of server/ finds none; server/replitAuth.ts:146-155 uses only sub, email, name and role claims). Login forces a fresh prompt (server/replitAuth.ts:176 prompt: login consent) but sets no max_age and nothing verifies the result. Administrative and impersonation routes (server/routes.ts:403) require no stronger or more recent authentication than ordinary ones.
Gap: The app cannot tell whether MFA was performed or how recently, and has no documented fallback assumption.
Fix: Request and record amr/acr/auth_time (Entra authentication context or claims), require MFA and recent authentication for admin, impersonation and retention actions, and document the fallback.

Requirement text: Verify that the user's session inactivity timeout and absolute maximum session lifetime are documented, are appropriate in combination with other controls, and that the documentation includes justification for any deviations from NIST SP 800-63B re-authentication requirements.
Evidence or reason: No session policy found in FOLLOW_UPS.md, replit.md or security/ASVS_LEVEL2.md; only a hard-coded 7 day TTL at server/replitAuth.ts:37 (.docx briefings not inspected)
Gap: The inactivity timeout and absolute lifetime are not documented or justified; the only value is a 7 day constant in code.
Fix: Write a short session policy (idle, absolute, re-authentication, justification against NIST 800-63B) and make the code match it.

Requirement text: Verify that the documentation defines how many concurrent (parallel) sessions are allowed for one account as well as the intended behaviors and actions to be taken when the maximum number of active sessions is reached.
