Evidence or reason: No concurrent-session limit or documentation anywhere: server/replitAuth.ts:36-56 sets no per-user limit and no code lists sessions per user
Gap: The number of concurrent sessions per account and the behaviour at the limit are neither defined nor documented or enforced.
Fix: Decide and document the policy (for example unlimited with visibility, or a cap) and record it in the session policy.

Requirement text: Verify that all systems that create and manage user sessions as part of a federated identity management ecosystem (such as SSO systems) are documented along with controls to coordinate session lifetimes, termination, and any other conditions that require re-authentication.
Evidence or reason: No documentation of the IdP/RP session relationship; code shows RP session independent of IdP session (server/replitAuth.ts:36-56, 229-243) and no back-channel logout
Gap: The federated ecosystem (customer IdP, Capera session, any proxy or SSO portal) and how lifetimes and termination are coordinated are not documented.
Fix: Document the IdP and Capera session lifetimes, logout and re-authentication triggers once the customer IdP is chosen.

Requirement text: Verify that the application performs all session token verification using a trusted, backend service.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): As V6.3.2; and the gate runs the checks on every route. Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: A single environment variable switches off all session verification and signs everyone in as an admin-level user; nothing prevents it reaching production.

Requirement text: Verify that the application uses either self-contained or reference tokens that are dynamically generated for session management, i.e. not using static API secrets and keys.
Evidence or reason: Session IDs are generated per session by express-session (no custom genid: server/replitAuth.ts:45-55; node_modules/express-session/index.js:94,527). No Bearer or API-key authentication of users: only outbound Authorization header in server/services/emailService.ts:140,159

Requirement text: Verify that if reference tokens are used to represent user sessions, they are unique and generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) and possess at least 128 bits of entropy.
Evidence or reason: Default generator uid(24) = 24 bytes from crypto randomBytes (192 bits): node_modules/express-session/index.js:527; node_modules/uid-safe/index.js:76; no genid override at server/replitAuth.ts:45-55

Requirement text: Verify that the application generates a new session token on user authentication, including re-authentication, and terminates the current session token.
Evidence or reason: Callback uses passport.authenticate without keepSessionInfo (server/replitAuth.ts:181-186); passport 0.7 logIn calls req.session.regenerate which destroys the old session: node_modules/passport/lib/sessionmanager.js:28; node_modules/passport/lib/middleware/authenticate.js:265. Re-authentication goes through the same /api/login -> callback path (server/replitAuth.ts:174-186). Dev shortcut does not regenerate but is dev-only (:117-122)

Requirement text: Verify that there is an inactivity timeout such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Idle limit 60 minutes (SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES). Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: There is no inactivity timeout chosen from risk analysis; a stolen or left-open session stays valid for up to a week of activity.

Requirement text: Verify that there is an absolute maximum session lifetime such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Absolute limit 12 hours (SESSION_ABSOLUTE_HOURS); older sessions sign in again once. Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: No absolute session lifetime is enforced by Capera; a session lasts as long as the IdP refresh token (possibly months) and some routes never check expiry.

Requirement text: Verify that when session termination is triggered (such as logout or expiration), the application disallows any further use of the session. For reference tokens or stateful sessions, this means invalidating the session data at the application backend. Applications using self-contained tokens will need a solution such as maintaining a list of terminated tokens, disallowing tokens produced before a per-user date and time or rotating a per-user signing key.
Evidence or reason: /api/logout calls req.logout (server/replitAuth.ts:188-197): passport saves then regenerates, destroying the server-side session (node_modules/passport/lib/sessionmanager.js:64-93); expired rows are pruned by connect-pg-simple (default prune) and honoured by TTL (server/replitAuth.ts:37-44). Then RP-initiated IdP logout. Caveats: refresh token not revoked at IdP (but is discarded with the session); logout is GET; dev shortcut does not destroy (dev only, :134)

Requirement text: Verify that the application terminates all active sessions when a user account is disabled or deleted (such as an employee leaving the company).
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): A closed account is refused on every /api route (checked at most once a minute), and a failed check refuses rather than allows. Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: A leaver or disabled user with a live session can keep calling about 79 assessment, allocation and training endpoints (including assessment sign-off) and no session is actually terminated.
Gap: Sessions are not actively ended when an account is disabled; relies on the one-minute check.
Fix: Apply one global authentication middleware (expiry, refresh, closed-account check, fail closed) to all /api routes except login and callback, and delete the user's rows from the sessions table on archive or anonymise.

Requirement text: Verify that the application gives the option to terminate all other active sessions after a successful change or removal of any authentication factor (including password change via reset or recovery and, if present, an MFA settings update).
Evidence or reason: Capera has no password, MFA or recovery management; authentication is delegated entirely to the OIDC provider (server/replitAuth.ts:101-198; passport-local is listed in package.json but unused in server/). The IdP must provide: option to sign out other sessions after password or MFA change, and revoke refresh tokens (for Entra: revoke sessions, Continuous Access Evaluation)

Requirement text: Verify that all pages that require authentication have easy and visible access to logout functionality.
Evidence or reason: All authenticated screens render inside the sidebar layout (client/src/App.tsx:206-234) whose user menu has Sign out (client/src/components/AppSidebar.tsx:99); the account-closed screen has a Sign out link (client/src/App.tsx:189). Two clicks via the user menu, and the sidebar is collapsible on narrow screens

Requirement text: Verify that application administrators are able to terminate active sessions for an individual user or for all users.
Evidence or reason: No endpoint or UI lists or deletes rows of the sessions table (shared/schema.ts:10 defines it; used only by connect-pg-simple at server/replitAuth.ts:39-44); grep of server/ finds no session administration
Gap: Administrators cannot terminate one user's or all users' sessions from Capera, only archive the account (which is not enforced on every route).
Fix: Add admin endpoints that delete sessions for a user (matching sess->passport->user->claims->sub) or all, and call them on archive, role removal and incident response.

Requirement text: Verify that the application requires full re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes which may affect authentication such as email address, phone number, MFA configuration, or other information used in account recovery.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): A person can no longer change their own email; only administrators can; only a super administrator or developer can act as one. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Email (an identity-linking attribute) can be changed with only the existing session, with no re-authentication; admins can change others' emails likewise. Separately, any admin or developer can impersonate any user including super_admin with no re-authentication, reason, time limit or notice, and trainingPerm and actingUser then apply the target role.
Gap: No fresh sign-in is demanded before an administrator changes email, roles or starts acting as someone.
Fix: Strip email and providerSub from self-service updates; require recent IdP authentication for admin email/role changes and for starting impersonation, block impersonating higher-privileged roles, add reason and an expiry (for example 30 minutes), and audit reads made while impersonating.

Requirement text: Verify that users are able to view and (having authenticated again with at least one factor) terminate any or all currently active sessions.
Evidence or reason: No user-facing list of active sessions or terminate-all function in server/ or client/src (client logout is only window.location /api/logout: client/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:66-68)
Gap: Users cannot see or end their other sessions; only the current session can be ended.
Fix: Add a My sessions page listing the user's sessions with end-one and end-all-others actions, requiring a fresh sign-in first.

Requirement text: Verify that session lifetime and termination between Relying Parties (RPs) and Identity Providers (IdPs) behave as documented, requiring re-authentication as necessary such as when the maximum time between IdP authentication events is reached.
Evidence or reason: Partial coupling: expires_at taken from ID token exp and refreshed via refresh token, a failed refresh returns 401 (server/replitAuth.ts:62-65, 220-243), but routes without isAuthenticated skip it (server/routes.ts:237-292, 79 routes); no max_age/auth_time use, no back-channel or front-channel logout endpoint (grep of server/), so IdP sign-out or revocation does not end Capera sessions; behaviour is not documented (see V7.1.3)
Gap: Capera sessions are not tied to a maximum time between IdP authentications and IdP logout or disablement does not terminate them, so behaviour cannot match a documented policy.
Fix: Enforce an absolute lifetime and a global refresh/expiry check (V7.3.2, V7.4.2), and add OIDC back-channel logout if the customer IdP supports it.

Requirement text: Verify that creation of a session requires either the user's consent or an explicit action, preventing the creation of new application sessions without user interaction.
Evidence or reason: Sessions are only created by the /api/login -> callback flow started by the user clicking Sign in (client/src/pages/Landing.tsx:71; client/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:62-64), with prompt login consent forcing interaction (server/replitAuth.ts:174-179); no client code redirects to /api/login on 401 (only those two references). Counter-example: failureRedirect to /api/login (:184) restarts the flow but the prompt still needs user action. Verify the combined prompt value is accepted by the customer IdP

Requirement text: Verify that authorization documentation defines rules for restricting function-level and data-specific access based on consumer permissions and resource attributes.
Evidence or reason: Rules exist only as code and scattered comments: shared/trainingPermissions.ts:1-9 (training matrix, editable at /api/training-permissions); server/services/performance.ts:236-245 and 303-311 (appraisal access rules); server/performanceRoutes.ts:6-8; FOLLOW_UPS.md:136; replit.md:18-20 (one-paragraph RBAC summary). No authorization document or role x function x data-scope matrix exists.
Gap: There is no single authorization document stating, per role, which functions are allowed and which records they may touch (own record, direct reports, allocated candidates, allocated assessors, whole company). The code is inconsistent on exactly these data-scope rules (managers, assessors and verifiers see company-wide data in many routes), so reviewers cannot tell what is intended versus a bug.
Fix: Write and maintain a role x function x data-scope matrix (admin, super_admin, developer, manager, appraiser, assessor, internal_verifier, trainer roles, candidate), reviewed by the business and used as the test oracle for authorization tests.

Requirement text: Verify that authorization documentation defines rules for field-level access restrictions (both read and write) based on consumer permissions and resource attributes. Note that these rules might depend on other attribute values of the relevant data object, such as state or status.
Evidence or reason: Field-level rules are implemented and commented for the appraisal only: server/services/performance.ts:303-325 (employee never sees potentialRating/calibrationNote/scores; manager side hidden until shared; supervisor does not see ratings), 741-785 (360 anonymity, minimum raters); cost hiding at server/routes.ts:213-221 (stripCostForViewer); Talent Score admin-only at server/performanceRoutes.ts:127-136. Nothing documents field read/write rules for the users record, bookings, assessments, certificates.
Gap: Field-level read and write rules are not documented outside the appraisal module, and the users record (date of birth, retention hold reason, CV/avatar keys), bookings (status, cost) and assessments have no stated rule for who may read or write which field.
Fix: Extend the authorization document with a field table for users, bookings, assessments, evidence and certificates (read/write by role and record state), then drive the response-shaping and write allow-lists from it.

Requirement text: Verify that the application ensures that function-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Sign-in required on every route by default. Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: Several sensitive read routes (succession plans, everyone's skills, certificates, expiry data) need only a sign-in, not a role. A large block of routes skips isAuthenticated, so a person who has left, or whose token has expired, can still use assessor, verifier and booking functions via a live session cookie. An ordinary admin can promote themselves or others to super_admin through PATCH /api/users/:id.
Gap: Some read routes (succession plans, everyone's skills, certificates, expiry data) still need only a sign-in, not a role.
Fix: Mount isAuthenticated once on all of /api after setupAuth (deny by default), put explicit role/permission gates on succession plans, user-skills, certificates and AI routes, and make PATCH /api/users/:id apply the same privileged-role rule as user creation.

Requirement text: Verify that the application ensures that data-specific access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific data items to mitigate insecure direct object reference (IDOR) and broken object level authorization (BOLA).
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Per-record checks added for CVs, assessments, assessment feedback, evidence lists and downloads, self-assessments and listing one person's assessments: the person, an administrator, their assessor, a verifier allocated to that assessor, or their manager (server/services/personAccess.ts). Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: A signed-in person can read other people's CVs and assessment feedback by id, and assessors, verifiers and managers can read or act on any person's competence, assessment and evidence data instead of only their own team or allocated candidates. The certificate ownership middleware can be bypassed by sending your own id in the body, which becomes exploitable as soon as the unimplemented certificate storage methods are filled in.
Gap: Many other record types (competence records, appraisals, skills, succession, certificates, reports) still check the role only.
Fix: Add per-record checks (self, direct report/supervisee, allocated candidate via candidate_allocations, allocated assessor via verifier_allocations, or admin) through one shared helper used by every :id or userId-filtered route, remove the body.userId fallback, and add authorization tests per role against these routes.

Requirement text: Verify that the application ensures that field-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific fields to mitigate broken object property level authorization (BOPLA).
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): User and booking updates are field-restricted by who is asking; the top two roles can only be given by a super administrator. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Writes are not field-restricted on user and booking updates, so a person can self-confirm a course booking as completed, edit their own retention hold or email, and an admin can create a super admin. Reads return whole records (date of birth, internal retention notes) to roles and to the data subject that do not need those fields.
Gap: Other update routes; responses still return whole records (V15.3.1).
Fix: Replace spread-the-body updates with per-role allow-listed Zod schemas (users: self vs admin vs HR; bookings: owner may only cancel), and add a response mapper per role that removes internal fields (retention*, *ObjectKey, providerSub, dateOfBirth where not needed).

Requirement text: Verify that the application enforces authorization rules at a trusted service layer and doesn't rely on controls that an untrusted consumer could manipulate, such as client-side JavaScript.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Closed by default for sign-in; a route that forgets its own check is still refused to strangers. Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: Authorization is server side, but because every route has to opt in, new or forgotten routes are open by default and several handlers check only the primary role, so behaviour differs from the effective-roles model the UI shows.
Gap: Role and record checks are still per route, and some use the primary role only.
Fix: Add an authenticated-by-default router for /api with an explicit public-route allow-list, and route all handler role checks through one effective-roles helper.

Requirement text: Verify that multi-tenant applications use cross-tenant controls to ensure consumer operations will never affect tenants with which they do not have permissions to interact.
Evidence or reason: Single organisation per deployment: no tenant or organisation key in shared/schema.ts (searched for tenant, organisationId, orgId, companyId: only contractCompanyId, which groups contractors inside one organisation, schema.ts:89); licence tier is a per-deployment environment setting (server/services/licence.ts:6). Caveat: if the hosting model ever becomes one shared instance for several customers, this becomes not_met (every query is unscoped, so it is a large change).

Requirement text: Verify that self-contained tokens are validated using their digital signature or MAC to protect against tampering before accepting the token's contents.
Evidence or reason: The only self-contained tokens the app handles are the provider's ID tokens, validated by openid-client/oauth4webapi before use: node_modules/oauth4webapi/build/index.js:1240 and 1696-1735 (signature and header checks); consumed at server/replitAuth.ts:62,152. The app issues no JWTs and accepts none from clients; sessions are opaque IDs in Postgres (server/replitAuth.ts:36-56).

Requirement text: Verify that only algorithms on an allowlist can be used to create and verify self-contained tokens, for a given context. The allowlist must include the permitted algorithms, ideally only either symmetric or asymmetric algorithms, and must not include the 'None' algorithm. If both symmetric and asymmetric must be supported, additional controls will be needed to prevent key confusion.
Evidence or reason: Allowed algorithm is checked in node_modules/oauth4webapi/build/index.js:1991-2016: client setting if present, else the issuer metadata list, else RS256. The application sets no id_token_signed_response_alg (server/replitAuth.ts:28-31 calls discovery with defaults), so the allowlist is whatever the trusted issuer advertises. No 'none' acceptance observed for Replit or Entra metadata.
Gap: The algorithm allowlist is not pinned in the application; it relies on issuer metadata.
Fix: Pass id_token_signed_response_alg: 'RS256' in the discovery client metadata.

Requirement text: Verify that key material that is used to validate self-contained tokens is from trusted pre-configured sources for the token issuer, preventing attackers from specifying untrusted sources and keys. For JWTs and other JWS structures, headers such as 'jku', 'x5u', and 'jwk' must be validated against an allowlist of trusted sources.
Evidence or reason: Keys come only from jwks_uri in metadata discovered from the pre-configured ISSUER_URL (server/replitAuth.ts:26-34; node_modules/oauth4webapi/build/index.js:1573,1060-1090); jku, x5u and embedded jwk headers are not used. Deployment note: ISSUER_URL must be the single-tenant Entra authority, not a multi-tenant common endpoint.

Requirement text: Verify that, if a validity time span is present in the token data, the token and its content are accepted only if the verification time is within this validity time span. For example, for JWTs, the claims 'nbf' and 'exp' must be verified.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Token expiry is checked on every /api route. Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: Token content (claims) stays accepted after expiry on those routes, for the whole 7-day session.

Requirement text: Verify that the service receiving a token validates the token to be the correct type and is meant for the intended purpose before accepting the token's contents. For example, only access tokens can be accepted for authorization decisions and only ID Tokens can be used for proving user authentication.
Evidence or reason: Identity is taken only from the ID token claims returned by the token endpoint (server/replitAuth.ts:62,146-155). The stored access token is never used for an authorisation decision and the app parses no client-supplied bearer token (no Authorization-header handling in server/ other than outbound email calls, server/services/emailService.ts:140,159). The library requires an id_token in the code-grant response (node_modules/oauth4webapi/build/index.js:1229-1240).

Requirement text: Verify that the service only accepts tokens which are intended for use with that service (audience). For JWTs, this can be achieved by validating the 'aud' claim against an allowlist defined in the service.
Evidence or reason: The ID token audience is validated against the configured client id: node_modules/oauth4webapi/build/index.js:1276-1291; client id passed at server/replitAuth.ts:30 (REPL_ID). Deployment note: the Entra application (client) id must be configured there.

Requirement text: Verify that, if a token issuer uses the same private key for issuing tokens to different audiences, the issued tokens contain an audience restriction that uniquely identifies the intended audiences. This will prevent a token from being reused with an unintended audience. If the audience identifier is dynamically provisioned, the token issuer must validate these audiences in order to make sure that they do not result in audience impersonation.
Evidence or reason: The application is not a token issuer: no JWT or signed-token creation anywhere in server/ (no jsonwebtoken/jose use); sessions are opaque IDs signed by express-session (server/replitAuth.ts:45-55).

Requirement text: Verify that tokens are only sent to components that strictly need them. For example, when using a backend-for-frontend pattern for browser-based JavaScript applications, access and refresh tokens shall only be accessible for the backend.
Evidence or reason: Tokens are kept in the server-side session (server/replitAuth.ts:58-66, 171-172); no other server or client file references access_token, refresh_token or id_token (grep); /api/auth/user returns the database user row, not req.user (server/routes.ts:358-395). Note tokens are stored unencrypted in the sessions table

Requirement text: Verify that the client only accepts values from the authorization server (such as the authorization code or ID Token) if these values result from an authorization flow that was initiated by the same user agent session and transaction. This requires that client-generated secrets, such as the proof key for code exchange (PKCE) 'code_verifier', 'state' or OIDC 'nonce', are not guessable, are specific to the transaction, and are securely bound to both the client and the user agent session in which the transaction was started.
Evidence or reason: PKCE code_verifier is random and stored server-side in the user's own session before the redirect (node_modules/openid-client/build/passport.js:118,144,158) and read only from that session on callback (:183,211); the session is regenerated at login (V7.2.4). Parallel logins in two tabs share one session key (benign overwrite)

Requirement text: Verify that, if the code flow is used, the OAuth client has protection against browser-based request forgery attacks, commonly known as cross-site request forgery (CSRF), which trigger token requests, either by using proof key for code exchange (PKCE) functionality or checking the 'state' parameter that was sent in the authorization request.
Evidence or reason: PKCE with S256 is always sent and verified (node_modules/openid-client/build/passport.js:118-121, 211); a state value is added if the IdP does not advertise PKCE and checked on callback (:122-125, 213)

Requirement text: Verify that, if the OAuth client can interact with more than one authorization server, it has a defense against mix-up attacks. For example, it could require that the authorization server return the 'iss' parameter value and validate it in the authorization response and the token response.
Evidence or reason: Single fixed issuer from ISSUER_URL, one shared config for all strategies (server/replitAuth.ts:26-34, 157-169); client never selects among authorization servers. The library also checks the iss response parameter when the IdP advertises it (node_modules/oauth4webapi/build/index.js:2051-2055)

Requirement text: Verify that the resource server only accepts access tokens that are intended for use with that service (audience). The audience may be included in a structured access token (such as the 'aud' claim in JWT), or it can be checked using the token introspection endpoint.
Evidence or reason: Capera is not an OAuth resource server: API authentication is the session cookie only (server/replitAuth.ts:213-259); no code reads an Authorization header (only outbound in server/services/emailService.ts:140,159)

Requirement text: Verify that the resource server enforces authorization decisions based on claims from the access token that define delegated authorization. If claims such as 'sub', 'scope', and 'authorization_details' are present, they must be part of the decision.
Evidence or reason: No access tokens are accepted by Capera; authorization uses server-side roles from the database (server/routes.ts:237-292), not token scopes

Requirement text: Verify that if an access control decision requires identifying a unique user from an access token (JWT or related token introspection response), the resource server identifies the user from claims that cannot be reassigned to other users. Typically, it means using a combination of 'iss' and 'sub' claims.
Evidence or reason: No access tokens are accepted; user identity comes from the session's ID token claims (see V10.5.2 for the identity-linking finding)

Requirement text: Verify that, if the resource server requires specific authentication strength, methods, or recentness, it verifies that the presented access token satisfies these constraints. For example, if present, using the OIDC 'acr', 'amr' and 'auth_time' claims respectively.
Evidence or reason: No access tokens are accepted and the server never reads acr, amr or auth_time (grep of server/); recentness is not required by any route today (see V7.5.1 for where it should be)

Requirement text: Verify that the authorization server validates redirect URIs based on a client-specific allowlist of pre-registered URIs using exact string comparison.
Evidence or reason: Capera is not an authorization server (no /authorize, /token, jwks or well-known routes: grep of server/ and shared/). Capera registers redirect https://DOMAIN/api/callback per domain (server/replitAuth.ts:157-169); the IdP must exact-match registered URIs and Capera's registration must list only those

Requirement text: Verify that, if the authorization server returns the authorization code in the authorization response, it can be used only once for a token request. For the second valid request with an authorization code that has already been used to issue an access token, the authorization server must reject a token request and revoke any issued tokens related to the authorization code.
Evidence or reason: Authorization-server behaviour; Capera has no AS endpoints. The customer IdP (for example Entra ID) must make codes single-use and revoke on reuse

Requirement text: Verify that the authorization code is short-lived. The maximum lifetime can be up to 10 minutes for L1 and L2 applications and up to 1 minute for L3 applications.
Evidence or reason: Authorization-server behaviour; Capera has no AS endpoints. IdP must keep authorization codes under 10 minutes

Requirement text: Verify that for a given client, the authorization server only allows the usage of grants that this client needs to use. Note that the grants 'token' (Implicit flow) and 'password' (Resource Owner Password Credentials flow) must no longer be used.
Evidence or reason: Authorization-server setting. Capera uses only the authorization code grant and refresh_token grant (server/replitAuth.ts:159-167, 237); the IdP app registration must disable implicit and password grants for it

Requirement text: Verify that the authorization server mitigates refresh token replay attacks for public clients, preferably using sender-constrained refresh tokens, i.e., Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP) or Certificate-Bound Access Tokens using mutual TLS (mTLS). For L1 and L2 applications, refresh token rotation may be used. If refresh token rotation is used, the authorization server must invalidate the refresh token after usage, and revoke all refresh tokens for that authorization if an already used and invalidated refresh token is provided.
Evidence or reason: Authorization-server behaviour; IdP must rotate or sender-constrain refresh tokens. Client side stores the new refresh token each refresh (server/replitAuth.ts:62-65) but parallel requests could refresh with the same token (race) and a refresh response without a new refresh token would overwrite it with undefined; test against the chosen IdP

Requirement text: Verify that, if the code grant is used, the authorization server mitigates authorization code interception attacks by requiring proof key for code exchange (PKCE). For authorization requests, the authorization server must require a valid 'code_challenge' value and must not accept a 'code_challenge_method' value of 'plain'. For a token request, it must require validation of the 'code_verifier' parameter.
Evidence or reason: Authorization-server enforcement; the Capera client always sends S256 challenge and verifier (node_modules/openid-client/build/passport.js:118-121, 211). IdP must require PKCE and reject plain for this client

Requirement text: Verify that if the authorization server supports unauthenticated dynamic client registration, it mitigates the risk of malicious client applications. It must validate client metadata such as any registered URIs, ensure the user's consent, and warn the user before processing an authorization request with an untrusted client application.
Evidence or reason: Capera has no authorization server and no dynamic client registration endpoint (grep of server/ finds no registration route); it uses one pre-registered client id (server/replitAuth.ts:28-31)

Requirement text: Verify that refresh tokens have an absolute expiration, including if sliding refresh token expiration is applied.
Evidence or reason: Authorization-server setting: IdP must set an absolute maximum refresh token lifetime. Capera does not cap it itself (see V7.3.2)

Requirement text: Verify that refresh tokens and reference access tokens can be revoked by an authorized user using the authorization server user interface, to mitigate the risk of malicious clients or stolen tokens.
Evidence or reason: IdP user interface must let users or administrators revoke refresh tokens (for Entra, My Apps and admin revoke sessions); Capera has no such UI and does not revoke at logout (server/replitAuth.ts:188-197)

Requirement text: Verify that confidential client is authenticated for client-to-authorized server backchannel requests such as token requests, pushed authorization requests (PAR), and token revocation requests.
Evidence or reason: The client is configured with only a client id and no client secret, private key or other client authentication, so token and refresh requests are unauthenticated public-client requests: server/replitAuth.ts:28-31 (discovery(issuer, REPL_ID) with no auth argument); refresh at :237
Gap: Capera is a server-side application that can hold a credential, but sends token and refresh requests without authenticating itself to the IdP.
Fix: Register Capera as a confidential client with the customer IdP and pass a client secret or private_key_jwt from the platform secret store to discovery().

Requirement text: Verify that the authorization server configuration only assigns the required scopes to the OAuth client.
Evidence or reason: IdP registration must grant only what Capera needs. Capera requests openid email profile offline_access (server/replitAuth.ts:163,177); no API or Graph permissions are used. Confirm offline_access is needed (it drives the long-lived refresh token)

Requirement text: Verify that the client (as the relying party) mitigates ID Token replay attacks. For example, by ensuring that the 'nonce' claim in the ID Token matches the 'nonce' value sent in the authentication request to the OpenID Provider (in OAuth2 refereed to as the authorization request sent to the authorization server).
Evidence or reason: No nonce is sent in the code flow: nonce only added when response_type contains id_token (node_modules/openid-client/build/passport.js:109-112), expectedNonce is undefined (:212) so the library rejects any ID token carrying a nonce (node_modules/oauth4webapi/build/index.js:1417-1424). Replay is mitigated instead by PKCE and the back-channel token response
Gap: ID token replay is mitigated only by PKCE binding, not by the nonce the requirement names; acceptable for code flow only if documented and the IdP supports PKCE.
Fix: Subclass or wrap the passport strategy to send a random nonce, store it with the verifier and pass expectedNonce, or record PKCE-only as the documented mitigation.

Requirement text: Verify that the client uniquely identifies the user from ID Token claims, usually the 'sub' claim, which cannot be reassigned to other users (for the scope of an identity provider).
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Role claims in a token are ignored; linking by email is limited as in V6.8.1. Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: Anyone who can present an email claim matching an existing user (for example an unverified or tenant-editable email attribute at the new IdP) takes over that account and its data, and a role claim can set privilege.
Gap: Same as V6.8.1.
Fix: Identify users only by issuer plus sub; make email re-linking a one-off, admin-approved migration using a pre-loaded mapping; require email_verified; ignore the role claim.

Requirement text: Verify that the client rejects attempts by a malicious authorization server to impersonate another authorization server through authorization server metadata. The client must reject authorization server metadata if the issuer URL in the authorization server metadata does not exactly match the pre-configured issuer URL expected by the client.
Evidence or reason: Issuer is pre-configured by ISSUER_URL and discovery throws if metadata issuer differs exactly (server/replitAuth.ts:26-34; node_modules/openid-client/build/index.js:286-297); ID token iss also checked (node_modules/oauth4webapi/build/index.js:1306-1314). Caveat: Entra common/organizations endpoints derive the expected issuer from tid (openid-client index.js:493), so the deployment must use a tenant-specific ISSUER_URL

Requirement text: Verify that the client validates that the ID Token is intended to be used for that client (audience) by checking that the 'aud' claim from the token is equal to the 'client_id' value for the client.
Evidence or reason: ID token aud must equal the client_id (REPL_ID) and azp is checked when aud has several values: node_modules/oauth4webapi/build/index.js:1236-1250, 1280-1295; client id at server/replitAuth.ts:30

Requirement text: Verify that, when using OIDC back-channel logout, the relying party mitigates denial of service through forced logout and cross-JWT confusion in the logout flow. The client must verify that the logout token is correctly typed with a value of 'logout+jwt', contains the 'event' claim with the correct member name, and does not contain a 'nonce' claim. Note that it is also recommended to have a short expiration (e.g., 2 minutes).
Evidence or reason: Capera does not implement OIDC back-channel logout: no logout_token or logout+jwt handling and no back-channel route (grep of server/); only RP-initiated /api/logout (server/replitAuth.ts:188-197). If it is added later, V10.5.5 applies; see V7.6.1

Requirement text: Verify that the OpenID Provider only allows values 'code', 'ciba', 'id_token', or 'id_token code' for response mode. Note that 'code' is preferred over 'id_token code' (the OIDC Hybrid flow), and 'token' (any Implicit flow) must not be used.
Evidence or reason: OpenID Provider setting. Capera uses the code response type (default, no response_type override: server/replitAuth.ts:159-167, 174-179); the IdP registration must disable implicit and hybrid flows for this client

Requirement text: Verify that the OpenID Provider mitigates denial of service through forced logout. By obtaining explicit confirmation from the end-user or, if present, validating parameters in the logout request (initiated by the relying party), such as the 'id_token_hint'.
Evidence or reason: OpenID Provider behaviour: IdP must confirm logout with the user or validate id_token_hint. Note Capera sends client_id and post_logout_redirect_uri (derived from request host) but no id_token_hint (server/replitAuth.ts:191-194), so the IdP will prompt; post_logout_redirect_uri must be registered at the IdP

Requirement text: Verify that the authorization server ensures that the user consents to each authorization request. If the identity of the client cannot be assured, the authorization server must always explicitly prompt the user for consent.
Evidence or reason: Authorization-server consent function; Capera sends prompt login consent on every sign-in (server/replitAuth.ts:176). For an enterprise IdP, administrator consent for the app should be used

Requirement text: Verify that when the authorization server prompts for user consent, it presents sufficient and clear information about what is being consented to. When applicable, this should include the nature of the requested authorizations (typically based on scope, resource server, Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) authorization details), the identity of the authorized application, and the lifetime of these authorizations.
Evidence or reason: The consent screen is shown by the IdP; Capera only supplies scope and client identity (server/replitAuth.ts:163,177). IdP must show app name, scopes and lifetime

Requirement text: Verify that the user can review, modify, and revoke consents which the user has granted through the authorization server.
Evidence or reason: Review and revoke of consents is an IdP user interface function; Capera has no consent store (grep of server/ and shared/)

Requirement text: Verify that there is a documented policy for management of cryptographic keys and a cryptographic key lifecycle that follows a key management standard such as NIST SP 800-57. This should include ensuring that keys are not overshared (for example, with more than two entities for shared secrets and more than one entity for private keys).
Evidence or reason: No key management policy in the repository (security/ contains only ASVS_LEVEL2.md). Secrets used by the app, all read from environment variables: SESSION_SECRET (server/replitAuth.ts:46), DATABASE_URL (server/db.ts:13), ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (server/services/aiCompetencyReview.ts:15), OPENAI_API_KEY (server/services/aiTheming.ts:6), SMTP_PASS/RESEND_API_KEY/SENDGRID_API_KEY (server/services/emailService.ts:62-115), OIDC client identity REPL_ID (replitAuth.ts:30). A .env file exists in the OneDrive-synced working folder (contents not read).
Gap: There is no documented policy or lifecycle (generation, storage, rotation, revocation, who may hold each key) for the secrets the application depends on.
Fix: Write a short key management policy and per-secret lifecycle table (owner, store in the company vault, rotation interval, rotation procedure, revocation) aligned to NIST SP 800-57, one secret per purpose and per environment.

Requirement text: Verify that a cryptographic inventory is performed, maintained, regularly updated, and includes all cryptographic keys, algorithms, and certificates used by the application. It must also document where keys can and cannot be used in the system, and the types of data that can and cannot be protected using the keys.
Evidence or reason: No cryptographic inventory exists. Findings from this review that belong in it: HMAC-SHA256 session cookie signature with one shared SESSION_SECRET (express-session 1.18.2, replitAuth.ts:46; node_modules/cookie-signature/index.js:20); 192-bit random session ids (node_modules/express-session/index.js:526-527); OIDC via openid-client 6.8.0 (replitAuth.ts:1) including ID token validation and refresh tokens; randomUUID object keys (server/services/objectStorage.ts:29); randomInt certificate numbers (server/services/elearningCertificates.ts:73-76); TLS to Anthropic, OpenAI, Resend, SendGrid, SMTP and Postgres; no application-level encryption and no password hashing; OIDC access and refresh tokens are stored in the sessions table (replitAuth.ts:58-66).
Gap: There is no maintained list of keys, algorithms and certificates, where each may be used, or what data each protects.
Fix: Create the inventory from the findings listed here, keep it in the repository next to the key management policy and review it each release.

Requirement text: Verify that industry-validated implementations (including libraries and hardware-accelerated implementations) are used for cryptographic operations.
Evidence or reason: All cryptography comes from Node's crypto module or well-known libraries: randomUUID/randomInt only (server/services/objectStorage.ts:2,29; server/services/elearningCertificates.ts:1,75; server/storage.ts:244; server/localDevDb.ts:2), session signing by express-session/cookie-signature (node_modules/cookie-signature/index.js:20), OIDC and token validation by openid-client (server/replitAuth.ts:1). A search of server/, shared/ and client/src found no hand-written crypto, createHash, createCipher, md5 or sha1. Math.random appears only for non-security uses (server/routes.ts:1054 placeholder file name, 8404-8420 demo data, server/services/performance.ts:773 display shuffle, client EvidenceUpload ids).

Requirement text: Verify that the application is designed with crypto agility such that random number, authenticated encryption, MAC, or hashing algorithms, key lengths, rounds, ciphers and modes can be reconfigured, upgraded, or swapped at any time, to protect against cryptographic breaks. Similarly, it must also be possible to replace keys and passwords and re-encrypt data. This will allow for seamless upgrades to post-quantum cryptography (PQC), once high-assurance implementations of approved PQC schemes or standards are widely available.
Evidence or reason: Algorithms are library defaults and can be upgraded by updating packages (package.json: express-session, openid-client, nodemailer); keys are environment variables (replitAuth.ts:46). express-session is given a single string secret, so rotating it logs everyone out; no documented procedure for replacing SESSION_SECRET, API keys or database credentials. There is no application-level encrypted data, so nothing needs re-encrypting.
Gap: Secret rotation is not designed in: one session secret only, no tested or documented way to replace secrets without an outage.
Fix: Accept a list of session secrets (new first, old kept for the session lifetime) and write and test a rotation runbook for every secret.

Requirement text: Verify that all cryptographic primitives utilize a minimum of 128-bits of security based on the algorithm, key size, and configuration. For example, a 256-bit ECC key provides roughly 128 bits of security where RSA requires a 3072-bit key to achieve 128 bits of security.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): The server refuses to start in production without a SESSION_SECRET of at least 32 characters. Tested by: run: refused with a short secret. Original finding: Nothing stops the deployment starting with a short or guessable SESSION_SECRET, which would let someone forge session cookies, and the signature strength then depends on that secret.

Requirement text: Verify that insecure block modes (e.g., ECB) and weak padding schemes (e.g., PKCS#1 v1.5) are not used.
Evidence or reason: The application performs no block-cipher encryption: no createCipher/createCipheriv, no subtle.encrypt in server/, shared/ or client/src (searched). Encryption at rest of the database and object storage is a platform matter (see V11.1.1).

Requirement text: Verify that only approved ciphers and modes such as AES with GCM are used.
Evidence or reason: No application-level encryption exists (same search as V11.3.1). Cipher choice for storage and transport is the platform's, to be AES-GCM or equivalent.

Requirement text: Verify that encrypted data is protected against unauthorized modification preferably by using an approved authenticated encryption method or by combining an approved encryption method with an approved MAC algorithm.
Evidence or reason: The app does not encrypt data itself, so there is no encrypted data for it to authenticate. The session cookie is protected by an HMAC signature (node_modules/cookie-signature/index.js:20). Note for the platform review: OIDC access and refresh tokens sit in plaintext in the sessions table (server/replitAuth.ts:58-66, store at 39-44), so database-level encryption and access control matter.

Requirement text: Verify that only approved hash functions are used for general cryptographic use cases, including digital signatures, HMAC, KDF, and random bit generation. Disallowed hash functions, such as MD5, must not be used for any cryptographic purpose.
Evidence or reason: The application code calls no hash function at all (no createHash, md5, sha1 in server/, shared/ or client/src). The only hashing in the dependency path is HMAC-SHA256 for the session cookie (node_modules/cookie-signature/index.js:20) and the signature algorithms inside openid-client for token validation. nanoid in server/vite.ts:7,59 is a dev-server cache-buster only.

Requirement text: Verify that passwords are stored using an approved, computationally intensive, key derivation function (also known as a "password hashing function"), with parameter settings configured based on current guidance. The settings should balance security and performance to make brute-force attacks sufficiently challenging for the required level of security.
Evidence or reason: The application stores no passwords: sign-in is delegated to the OIDC provider (server/replitAuth.ts:1-9, 138-169); there is no password column in shared/schema.ts and passport-local is listed in package.json but never imported (no LocalStrategy anywhere in server/). The OIDC provider must meet this requirement for the sign-in credentials.

Requirement text: Verify that hash functions used in digital signatures, as part of data authentication or data integrity are collision resistant and have appropriate bit-lengths. If collision resistance is required, the output length must be at least 256 bits. If only resistance to second pre-image attacks is required, the output length must be at least 128 bits.
Evidence or reason: The only integrity hash in use is HMAC-SHA256 (256-bit output) on the session cookie (node_modules/cookie-signature/index.js:20); token signatures are validated by openid-client (server/replitAuth.ts:1,26-34,237). The application creates no digital signatures and no hashes for integrity of its own (see V11.4.1).

Requirement text: Verify that the application uses approved key derivation functions with key stretching parameters when deriving secret keys from passwords. The parameters in use must balance security and performance to prevent brute-force attacks from compromising the resulting cryptographic key.
Evidence or reason: No keys are derived from passwords anywhere (no scrypt, pbkdf2, argon2, hkdf in server/, shared/ or client/src); there are no password-protected exports or encrypted files.

Requirement text: Verify that all random numbers and strings which are intended to be non-guessable must be generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) and have at least 128 bits of entropy. Note that UUIDs do not respect this condition.
Evidence or reason: Session ids: uid-safe 24 random bytes = 192 bits (node_modules/express-session/index.js:526-527). OIDC state/nonce/PKCE by openid-client (server/replitAuth.ts:159-167). Object-store keys use randomUUID (server/services/objectStorage.ts:29), a UUID which ASVS says does not count as 128 bits, though no route accepts a key from a caller so they are not bearer secrets. Certificate numbers are 30 bits (server/services/elearningCertificates.ts:73-77), identifiers behind login only. server/routes.ts:1054 builds a placeholder URL with Math.random, not used for security.
Gap: Nothing guessable currently grants access, but object keys and certificate numbers do not reach 128 bits of CSPRNG output, so they could not safely be used as links or verification codes later.
Fix: Use crypto.randomBytes(16) hex for object keys, and give any future public certificate verification a separate 128-bit random token.

Requirement text: Verify that only approved cryptographic algorithms and modes of operation are used for key generation and seeding, and digital signature generation and verification. Key generation algorithms must not generate insecure keys vulnerable to known attacks, for example, RSA keys which are vulnerable to Fermat factorization.
Evidence or reason: The application generates no cryptographic keys and creates or verifies no digital signatures itself (no generateKeyPair, createSign, createVerify in server/ or shared/); the session secret is supplied by the operator. Token verification is inside openid-client.

Requirement text: Verify that only the latest recommended versions of the TLS protocol are enabled, such as TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. The latest version of the TLS protocol must be the preferred option.
Evidence or reason: The app serves plain HTTP on 0.0.0.0:PORT (server/index.ts:87-100; http createServer at server/routes.ts:6044, no https/tls options anywhere) and expects a TLS-terminating proxy (trust proxy 1, server/replitAuth.ts:102). Platform must provide: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 only (1.3 preferred, SSLv3/TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled) on the company load balancer or reverse proxy, and plain HTTP reachable only from that proxy.

Requirement text: Verify that only recommended cipher suites are enabled, with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy.
Evidence or reason: Cipher suite selection is not in the application (no tls options in server/). Platform must provide: a current recommended cipher list with the strongest preferred (forward-secret ECDHE/AEAD suites) on the TLS terminator, and Node 20+ defaults for the app's outbound connections.

Requirement text: Verify that the application validates that mTLS client certificates are trusted before using the certificate identity for authentication or authorization.
Evidence or reason: No mutual TLS or client-certificate authentication exists: nothing in server/ uses requestCert, client certificates or certificate identity for authentication or authorization (searched); users sign in through OIDC (server/replitAuth.ts:138-169). If the company terminates mTLS in front of the app, that is the platform's check.

Section: HTTPS Communication with External Facing Services
Requirement text: Verify that TLS is used for all connectivity between a client and external facing, HTTP-based services, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Strict-Transport-Security is sent in production; the third-party Replit script is removed. Tested by: by reading the code. Original finding: HSTS and the redirect are not set by the app, so protection against downgrade depends on the company proxy being configured for it. A script from replit.com runs on every page of the app, which can read all data on the page if that host were compromised.
Gap: Fonts still from Google; the redirect from http to https is for the platform.
Fix: Remove the replit dev banner script and self-host fonts; set HSTS (helmet) and require x-forwarded-proto https in production; platform must also redirect HTTP to HTTPS and send HSTS.

Section: HTTPS Communication with External Facing Services
Requirement text: Verify that external facing services use publicly trusted TLS certificates.
Evidence or reason: Certificates are issued and installed on the company's TLS terminator, not in the app (server/index.ts:87-100 serves HTTP only). Platform must provide a certificate that the users' browsers trust (publicly trusted CA if reachable from outside the company, or the company's enterprise CA for internal-only access), with automated renewal.

Section: General Service to Service Communication Security
Requirement text: Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application, including monitoring systems, management tools, remote access and SSH, middleware, databases, mainframes, partner systems, or external APIs. The server must not fall back to insecure or unencrypted protocols.
Evidence or reason: HTTPS to AI providers (Anthropic SDK server/services/aiCompetencyReview.ts:18, OpenAI SDK aiTheming.ts:6), to Resend and SendGrid (server/services/emailService.ts:136,155), to the OIDC issuer (server/replitAuth.ts:29) and Neon over wss (server/db.ts:8, 26-31). Not enforced: SMTP defaults to port 587 with secure=false and no requireTLS (emailService.ts:56-66, 30-40), so STARTTLS is opportunistic and can fall back to plaintext carrying personal data; PostgreSQL (db.ts:30-33) and the session store (replitAuth.ts:40) use only DATABASE_URL, no ssl setting, so TLS happens only if the URL says so; object storage is the Replit-only SDK (server/services/objectStorage.ts:1-20) and will be replaced by the company's store.
Gap: Encryption of the database link and of outbound email is left to configuration, and a misconfigured SMTP or database URL would silently send personal data unencrypted.
Fix: Set requireTLS for SMTP, require ssl (verify-full) for the database and session store with a start-up check in production, and confirm the replacement object store client uses https only.

Section: General Service to Service Communication Security
Requirement text: Verify that TLS clients validate certificates received before communicating with a TLS server.
Evidence or reason: No override of certificate validation in the code: no rejectUnauthorized:false or NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED in server/, shared/ or package.json (searched), so HTTPS clients (OIDC, Anthropic, OpenAI, Resend, SendGrid) use Node's default validation. Database and SMTP validation depends on connection settings that the code does not fix (server/db.ts:30-33, emailService.ts:30-40). Trust of a company-internal CA needs NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, not set anywhere in the repository.
Gap: Validation is by default for HTTPS, but for the database and SMTP it depends on configuration that is not checked, and internal CA trust is undocumented.
Fix: Document and test the TLS settings for database and SMTP (verify-full, internal CA via NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) in the deployment guide and as start-up checks.

Section: General Service to Service Communication Security
Requirement text: Verify that TLS or another appropriate transport encryption mechanism used for all connectivity between internal, HTTP-based services within the application, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.
Evidence or reason: Capera is one process serving the API and the client (server/index.ts:84-87); there are no internal HTTP services or microservice calls in server/. Its database, email and AI connections are covered under V12.3.1.

Section: General Service to Service Communication Security
Requirement text: Verify that TLS connections between internal services use trusted certificates. Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the consuming service must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates.
Evidence or reason: No internal HTTP service-to-service connections exist (single process, see V12.3.3). If the company uses an internal CA for the database or object store, trusting only that CA is a deployment setting covered under V12.3.2.

Requirement text: Verify that all communication needs for the application are documented. This must include external services which the application relies upon and cases where an end user might be able to provide an external location to which the application will then connect.
Evidence or reason: replit.md:83-121 lists external dependencies (Neon, Resend, SendGrid, OpenAI); outbound calls actually found: server/services/emailService.ts:136,155 (Resend/SendGrid), SMTP_HOST env (emailService.ts:62), server/replitAuth.ts:29 (OIDC issuer), server/services/aiCompetencyReview.ts:18 and translationService.ts:90 (Anthropic), aiTheming.ts:6 (OpenAI), objectStorage.ts:1 (Replit object storage), client/index.html:7-9,14 (Google Fonts, replit.com script). No server code fetches a user-supplied URL (grep of fetch/http in server/).
Gap: The list in replit.md is stale and incomplete: it names OpenAI for translation but the code uses Anthropic, and it omits the OIDC issuer, object storage, Google Fonts and the replit.com browser script. There is no single communications inventory with protocol, direction, data sent and credentials.
Fix: Write a one-page communications inventory (destination, purpose, data sent, auth, who owns it) and state that no feature lets a user supply a server-side fetch target.

Requirement text: Verify that communications between backend application components that don't support the application's standard user session mechanism, including APIs, middleware, and data layers, are authenticated. Authentication must use individual service accounts, short-term tokens, or certificate-based authentication and not unchanging credentials such as passwords, API keys, or shared accounts with privileged access.
Evidence or reason: Backend components authenticate with long-lived static secrets read once at start-up: DATABASE_URL (server/db.ts:13,28-32), SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASS (emailService.ts:65-66), RESEND/SENDGRID keys (emailService.ts:84,101), ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (aiCompetencyReview.ts:18), OPENAI_API_KEY (aiTheming.ts:6), SESSION_SECRET (replitAuth.ts:46).
Gap: Every service credential is an unchanging password or API key held in the process environment; the DB pool is built once so a rotated or short-lived credential needs a restart; nothing supports certificate or token-based service identity.
Fix: Have the platform inject per-service short-lived or rotated credentials (vault dynamic DB creds, workload identity or mTLS for the database and storage) and make the pool re-read them; keep third-party API keys in the vault with a rotation schedule.

Requirement text: Verify that communications between backend application components, including local or operating system services, APIs, middleware, and data layers, are performed with accounts assigned the least necessary privileges.
Evidence or reason: One DATABASE_URL serves the running app (server/db.ts:28-32), session store (replitAuth.ts:40) and schema changes (drizzle.config.ts:10-12, npm run db:push at package.json:11). Nothing in the repo defines separate roles or grants; audit_events is written and also updated by the app (server/services/retention.ts:107-110).
Gap: The code assumes a single all-powerful database account for runtime and migrations; the audit table is not protected from UPDATE/DELETE at database level. Actual grants cannot be seen from the code.
Fix: Create separate migration and runtime DB roles (runtime without DDL, no UPDATE/DELETE on audit_events except the anonymisation routine) and document the grants.

Requirement text: Verify that if a credential has to be used for service authentication, the credential being used by the consumer is not a default credential (e.g., root/root or admin/admin).
Evidence or reason: Production path has no default credentials: SESSION_SECRET has no fallback (server/replitAuth.ts:46) and DATABASE_URL is mandatory (server/db.ts:13-17); EMAIL_FROM default is only a sender address (emailService.ts:59). The 'local-dev-only-secret' fallback (replitAuth.ts:118) is only inside the LOCAL_DEV_AUTH branch (see V13.4.2 for the missing production guard). A postgres:postgres@localhost string exists only in an unused scaffold under attached_assets/training-mgmt-scaffold/server/src/db.js:4, not in the runtime code.

Requirement text: Verify that an allowlist is used to define the external resources or systems with which the application is permitted to communicate (e.g., for outbound requests, data loads, or file access). This allowlist can be implemented at the application layer, web server, firewall, or a combination of different layers.
Evidence or reason: Application layer has no allowlist mechanism, but every outbound destination is fixed in code or set by operator env vars (emailService.ts:62,136,155; replitAuth.ts:29; SDK default hosts for Anthropic/OpenAI; objectStorage.ts) and no user-supplied URL is fetched by the server (grep of server/ shows fetch only in emailService.ts). The browser also loads fonts.googleapis.com and replit.com (client/index.html:7-14). Platform must enforce an egress allowlist (firewall or egress proxy) limited to the documented list: OIDC issuer, SMTP relay or Resend/SendGrid, Anthropic/OpenAI if AI is enabled, database, object store.

Requirement text: Verify that the web or application server is configured with an allowlist of resources or systems to which the server can send requests or load data or files from.
Evidence or reason: Same as V13.2.4: the Node process has no host-level outbound restrictions in the repo (no Dockerfile, network policy or proxy config exists; .replit:13-14 only sets the Replit port). The company container platform must apply a default-deny egress policy to the application namespace and permit only the documented destinations.

Requirement text: Verify that a secrets management solution, such as a key vault, is used to securely create, store, control access to, and destroy backend secrets. These could include passwords, key material, integrations with databases and third-party systems, keys and seeds for time-based tokens, other internal secrets, and API keys. Secrets must not be included in application source code or included in build artifacts. For an L3 application, this must involve a hardware-backed solution such as an HSM.
Evidence or reason: No secrets in source: grep for key/URL/token patterns across server/, shared/, client/src, scripts/ found none; .env is git-ignored (.gitignore:3) and untracked; secrets are read from process.env (replitAuth.ts:46, db.ts:13, emailService.ts:62-66, aiCompetencyReview.ts:18); client bundle exposes only VITE_DEMO_REQUEST_EMAIL (Landing.tsx:13); demo zips contain no .env. Counter-evidence: a live .env with a real database URL sits in the OneDrive-synced project folder, and FOLLOW_UPS.md:18 records that the Neon password has appeared in session logs and still needs rotating.
Gap: Secrets are handled correctly in code but there is no vault integration or documented create/rotate/destroy process, and a known-exposed database password has not been rotated; the working .env is cloud-synced by OneDrive.
Fix: Rotate the exposed database password now, move .env out of the synced folder, and have the company vault inject all secrets at runtime with a documented rotation process.

Requirement text: Verify that access to secret assets adheres to the principle of least privilege.
Evidence or reason: Code reads every secret from one process environment (single process holds DB, SMTP, AI and session secrets), so least privilege over who can read each secret is decided by the vault policy and container runtime, not the app. Platform must: scope each secret to the Capera workload only, restrict read access to named operators, enable access auditing, and keep secrets out of build logs and image layers.

Requirement text: Verify that the application is deployed either without any source control metadata, including the .git or .svn folders, or in a way that these folders are inaccessible both externally and to the application itself.
Evidence or reason: Static serving is limited to the build output: express.static(dist/public) in server/vite.ts:70-79, so .git is not reachable over HTTP; vite dev server denies dotfiles (vite.config.ts:35-38). Counter-evidence: no Dockerfile or .dockerignore exists, and the project root contains .git, .env, internal IP-provenance .docx briefings, 242 tracked attached_assets files, zips and logs (git ls-files | grep -c attached_assets = 242).
Gap: Nothing prevents a 'COPY . .' container build from packaging .git, .env, the internal IP briefings and attached_assets into the image, where the application process can read them.
Fix: Add a multi-stage Dockerfile that copies only dist and production node_modules, plus a .dockerignore excluding .git, .env, attached_assets, *.docx, *.zip and logs.

Requirement text: Verify that debug modes are disabled for all components in production environments to prevent exposure of debugging features and information leakage.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Server refuses to start with the sign-in bypass in production; demo and test endpoints (seed data, test users, test scenarios, storage test) answer "not found" in production unless ENABLE_DEMO_TOOLS=true. Tested by: run: refused; by reading the code for the endpoints. Original finding: A single environment variable (LOCAL_DEV_AUTH) switches off authentication entirely, nothing refuses to start in production with it set, and dev mode is the default when NODE_ENV is absent.

Requirement text: Verify that web servers do not expose directory listings to clients unless explicitly intended.
Evidence or reason: Only express.static is used (server/vite.ts:79) with no directory-listing middleware; serve-index is not in package.json dependencies; dist/public contains index.html so the root resolves to it; unmatched paths fall through to index.html (vite.ts:82-84).

Requirement text: Verify that using the HTTP TRACE method is not supported in production environments, to avoid potential information leakage.
Evidence or reason: Express has no TRACE handler and the app does not echo requests, but the catch-all app.use('*') at server/vite.ts:82-84 answers any method (including TRACE) with index.html. Behaviour at the company reverse proxy/WAF is outside the code. Needs a live check: curl -X TRACE against the deployed URL and confirm 405/403 at the edge.
Gap: TRACE is not explicitly rejected by the application; it returns the SPA page rather than an echo, so information leakage is unlikely, but this has not been tested.
Fix: Add a small middleware rejecting TRACE/TRACK with 405 and confirm the proxy blocks it.

Requirement text: Verify that documentation (such as for internal APIs) and monitoring endpoints are not exposed unless explicitly intended.
Evidence or reason: No API documentation, Swagger/OpenAPI, /metrics, /health or /debug routes exist (grep of server/*.ts for swagger|openapi|health|metrics|debug found none); the only routes are the application API and the static SPA (server/index.ts:62-81, vite.ts:70-84). Note for the platform team: there is no health endpoint for probes, so one will need to be added deliberately and kept minimal.

Requirement text: Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified and classified into protection levels. This includes data that is only encoded and therefore easily decoded, such as Base64 strings or the plaintext payload inside a JWT. Protection levels need to take into account any data protection and privacy regulations and standards which the application is required to comply with.
Evidence or reason: No data classification exists in the repo: security/ASVS_LEVEL2.md states the target only; FOLLOW_UPS.md:13 lists the DPIA as still to do. Sensitive fields are present (shared/schema.ts:39-41 dateOfBirth, companyNumber, vantageNumber; 57-60 CV; performance reviews, 360, Talent Score) with no stated protection levels.
Gap: Personal data (identity, date of birth, helicopter-travel number, CVs, appraisals, 360 feedback, Talent Score, email text) has not been inventoried or classified into protection levels, including data held in session JSON and logs.
Fix: Produce a data inventory and classification table (public/internal/personal/special-risk) covering tables, files, logs, sessions and email log, and complete the DPIA.

Requirement text: Verify that all sensitive data protection levels have a documented set of protection requirements. This must include (but not be limited to) requirements related to general encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, database-level encryption, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies to be used, and other confidentiality requirements.
Evidence or reason: No document defines per-level requirements for encryption, integrity, retention, logging, log access or database encryption (none in security/, FOLLOW_UPS.md, replit.md). Partial building blocks exist in code: retention routine (server/services/retention.ts:75-129) and audit redaction regex (server/services/auditLog.ts:46).
Gap: There is no written set of protection requirements per data level.
Fix: Write the protection requirements per level (encryption in transit/at rest, retention periods, log handling, access, backups) and cross-reference the platform controls.

Requirement text: Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields, and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information, such as an API key or session token.
Evidence or reason: Sensitive values travel in request bodies/headers: session is an httpOnly cookie (server/replitAuth.ts:50-54); talent search, imports and uploads are POST bodies (routes.ts:4525, 705, 1355). Searches of client/src and server/ for token/key/secret/password/email/dob in query strings found none; URLs carry only opaque UUIDs (e.g. AdminUsers.tsx:285-286, CompetenceBadgeQr.tsx:13). Search terms (audit log q, notification q) are in query strings but are not secrets.

Requirement text: Verify that the application prevents sensitive data from being cached in server components, such as load balancers and application caches, or ensures that the data is securely purged after use.
Evidence or reason: Server-side caches hold little personal data and expire: closedCache and nameCache 60 s (replitAuth.ts:202-209, auditLog.ts:105-113), OIDC config 1 h (replitAuth.ts:26-34). Counter-evidence: the sessions table stores the OIDC access and refresh tokens and email claims in clear (replitAuth.ts:58-66, 171-172); no Cache-Control is set on API responses, so a shared proxy or load balancer can apply its own rules; avatars/CVs are marked private with max-age 3600 (routes.ts:1339,1397) and SCORM files 86400 (routes.ts:5100).
Gap: Authenticated API responses carry no cache directives and tokens are stored unencrypted in the session table, so correct behaviour depends on the unconfigured proxy and database.
Fix: Add a global Cache-Control: no-store middleware for /api, and have the platform encrypt the DB at rest (optionally encrypt tokens in the session).

Requirement text: Verify that defined sensitive data is not sent to untrusted parties (e.g., user trackers) to prevent unwanted collection of data outside of the application's control.
Evidence or reason: No analytics/trackers found in client/src or index.html. Counter-evidence: every page load calls fonts.googleapis.com/fonts.gstatic.com (client/index.html:7-9, also in dist/public/index.html) and runs a third-party script from replit.com in the authenticated app origin (client/index.html:14, present in dist/public/index.html); candidate name and evidence file text/images are sent to Anthropic for AI review (routes.ts:7482-7500, aiCompetencyReview.ts:55) and user text to Anthropic for translation (routes.ts:6155-6262, translationService.ts:90) with no per-organisation switch other than leaving the API key unset.
Gap: User IP and browser data go to Google, a third-party Replit script executes with full access to the logged-in page, and personal data goes to an AI provider with no documented approval or opt-out.
Fix: Remove the replit.com banner script, self-host fonts, and make AI features an explicit per-organisation setting with the provider named in the data-protection documentation.

Requirement text: Verify that controls around sensitive data related to encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies, are implemented as defined in the documentation for the specific data's protection level.
Evidence or reason: Implemented controls: leaver anonymisation and retention hold (server/services/retention.ts:75-129), cascade removal of stored CV/avatar (retention.ts:113), audit redaction of secrets (auditLog.ts:46), account block for leavers (replitAuth.ts:203-259), performance/Talent Score admin-only. Not implemented or undecided: retention for the audit log (FOLLOW_UPS.md:114) and email log (FOLLOW_UPS.md:57); object deletion is best-effort (FOLLOW_UPS.md:29); session rows persist tokens; audit changes keep date of birth and other personal field values (auditLog.ts:66,75).
Gap: Because the required protection levels were never written down (V14.1.2), the controls cannot be shown to match them; retention of logs and email text, and deletion retry, are open.
Fix: After V14.1.2 is written, close the retention gaps (audit/email log periods, deletion retry, session purge) and mask personal field values in audit changes.

Requirement text: Verify that authenticated data is cleared from client storage, such as the browser DOM, after the client or session is terminated. The 'Clear-Site-Data' HTTP response header field may be able to help with this but the client-side should also be able to clear up if the server connection is not available when the session is terminated.
Evidence or reason: Sign-out is a full-page navigation to /api/logout (client/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:67, App.tsx:189), which discards in-memory React Query data; localStorage holds only theme settings. Counter-evidence: no Clear-Site-Data header is sent by the server (grep found none), no explicit queryClient.clear() exists, and API responses are not marked no-store so the browser HTTP cache may keep them.
Gap: Authenticated data is cleared only incidentally by the page reload; the browser cache may retain API responses after sign-out and nothing handles an unreachable server.
Fix: Send Clear-Site-Data: "cache", "storage" on logout, call queryClient.clear() on sign-out, and set no-store on API responses.

Requirement text: Verify that the application sets sufficient anti-caching HTTP response header fields (i.e., Cache-Control: no-store) so that sensitive data is not cached in browsers.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): API responses are sent no-store; CVs and downloads are private, no-store. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Most authenticated responses, including user records and CVs, can be stored in the browser cache, which matters on shared workstations.
Gap: Static page files and the avatar route keep their own cache rules.
Fix: Add app.use('/api', no-store middleware, and change CV/evidence/certificate downloads to no-store (keep private caching only for avatars if wanted).

Requirement text: Verify that data stored in browser storage (such as localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, or cookies) does not contain sensitive data, with the exception of session tokens.
Evidence or reason: Browser storage holds no personal data: localStorage keys are the colour theme (client/src/contexts/ThemeContext.tsx:30,54), sector theme (SectorThemeContext.tsx:73,106), a horizon number (pages/Briefing.tsx:253-254) and landing theme (pages/Landing.tsx:63,77); the only cookie written by script is sidebar open/closed state (components/ui/sidebar.tsx:86); the session cookie is httpOnly (server/replitAuth.ts:51). No sessionStorage, IndexedDB or query-cache persistence found.

Requirement text: Verify that application documentation defines risk based remediation time frames for 3rd party component versions with vulnerabilities and for updating libraries in general, to minimize the risk from these components.
