Evidence or reason: No remediation timeframes are documented (no security/ policy file beyond ASVS_LEVEL2.md; no SECURITY.md, Dependabot/Renovate config, or CI). package-lock.json exists but nothing sets how fast a critical/high advisory must be fixed.
Gap: There are no risk-based time limits for patching vulnerable third-party components or for routine library updates.
Fix: Add a one-page policy (for example critical 7 days, high 30, medium 90) and a monthly update cadence, with an owner.

Requirement text: Verify that an inventory catalog, such as software bill of materials (SBOM), is maintained of all third-party libraries in use, including verifying that components come from pre-defined, trusted, and continually maintained repositories.
Evidence or reason: A dependency inventory exists as 'Capera - open-source dependency licences.csv' (723 packages with versions and direct/indirect kind) and package-lock.json pins resolved versions. Not an SBOM format, not generated in CI (no CI exists), and no check that packages come from approved registries (no .npmrc/registry policy).
Gap: The inventory is a one-off licence list, not a maintained machine-readable SBOM, and there is no control that all packages come from trusted, maintained sources.
Fix: Generate a CycloneDX SBOM on each build (npx @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm), pin the registry in .npmrc, and review unmaintained packages (xlsx is stuck at 0.18.5).

Requirement text: Verify that the application documentation identifies functionality which is time-consuming or resource-demanding. This must include how to prevent a loss of availability due to overusing this functionality and how to avoid a situation where building a response takes longer than the consumer's timeout. Potential defenses may include asynchronous processing, using queues, and limiting parallel processes per user and per application.
Evidence or reason: No documentation identifies resource-heavy features. They exist in code: SCORM import unzip (routes.ts:5010-5075), 200 MB uploads (routes.ts:164-175), CSV/XLSX imports (routes.ts:565-585, services/lifecycleImport.ts, trainingMatrixImport.ts), PDF/DOCX extraction (services/documentExtraction.ts), AI calls (routes.ts:2412-2800, 6056-6262, 7482), compliance explorer and talent score (routes.ts:5360, 4525), 24-hour in-process jobs (server/index.ts:130-163).
Gap: There is no written list of expensive operations nor the limits, queueing or per-user concurrency chosen for them.
Fix: Document each heavy operation with its limit and timeout, and record which are queued or limited.

Requirement text: Verify that the application only contains components which have not breached the documented update and remediation time frames.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): npm audit fix (compatible versions only): 49 advisories down to 22, critical 0, high 21 down to 13. Tested by: npm audit. Original finding: The shipped dependency tree contains a critical and many high advisories, and there is no documented timeframe to measure it against; several are reachable from user input (multer uploads, body-parser, xlsx imports, nodemailer).
Gap: Remaining high ones need larger upgrades (drizzle-orm, zod, openai, nodemailer, tailwind build tools) or have no fix (xlsx); need testing one at a time. No policy yet on how fast advisories are fixed.
Fix: Update express, multer, nodemailer, ws, drizzle-orm, zod and openai to patched versions, replace xlsx with a maintained parser, run npm audit fix for transitive packages and retest.

Requirement text: Verify that the application has implemented defenses against loss of availability due to functionality which is time-consuming or resource-demanding, based on the documented security decisions and strategies for this.
Evidence or reason: Defences present: multer limits 10 MB / 200 MB (routes.ts:133-136,164-175); streaming upload to avoid memory exhaustion (routes.ts:139-160); decompressed-size cap with bounded concurrency for SCORM (routes.ts:5046-5075); audit page size clamp and CSV cap (auditLog.ts:201,220); account-closed lookups cached (replitAuth.ts:202-209). Counter-evidence: no rate limiting anywhere (grep for rate-limit found none); the zip-bomb check runs after each entry is fully inflated into memory (routes.ts:5052-5057); any signed-in user can trigger paid AI calls (routes.ts:6056-6110 ai-theme, 6155-6262 translation); no timeouts on outbound calls (emailService.ts:136,155, Anthropic/OpenAI SDK defaults); unbounded list endpoints such as getAllUsers (routes.ts:1167).
Gap: Heavy and costly endpoints have size limits but no rate limits, per-user concurrency limits, request or outbound timeouts, so one user or script can exhaust CPU, memory or AI spend.
Fix: Add express-rate-limit (global plus tighter on AI, import and upload routes), restrict AI endpoints by role, set server/request and outbound timeouts, and check zip entry sizes before inflating.

Requirement text: Verify that the production environment only includes functionality that is required for the application to function, and does not expose extraneous functionality such as test code, sample snippets, and development functionality.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Demo and test endpoints switched off in production by default; the sign-in bypass cannot run in production. Tested by: by reading the code. Original finding: Seed endpoints that create privileged test accounts, a no-authentication dev mode, dev-server tooling and unrelated sample assets are present in what would be deployed.
Gap: Dev-server tooling and unrelated files (internal briefings, .env) must be kept out of the production package (V13.4.1).
Fix: Gate or delete the seed/test-scenario routes outside development, lazy-import Vite only in development, drop attached_assets and test files from the image, and remove the banner script.

Requirement text: Verify that the application only returns the required subset of fields from a data object. For example, it should not return an entire data object, as some individual fields should not be accessible to users.
Evidence or reason: Whole user rows (including dateOfBirth, companyNumber, vantageNumber, cv keys, retentionHoldReason, providerSub; shared/schema.ts:21-70) are returned by: GET /api/users (routes.ts:1165-1168), GET /api/users/:id to any manager, assessor, verifier or training administrator for any person (routes.ts:1175-1190), GET /api/auth/user (358-368), the impersonate response (405-415), /api/auth/test-users (437-441), PATCH /api/users/:id response (1254-1281), upload responses (1325-1385). Newer modules do shape their output (e.g. Talent Score hidden from line managers, routes.ts:4530-4545).
Gap: Responses return the full user record, so date of birth, company number, internal storage keys and retention notes are exposed to roles that only need a name and job role.
Fix: Introduce explicit response DTOs per audience (self, admin, colleague/summary) and restrict the DOB/company number/vantage fields to HR/admin.

Requirement text: Verify that where the application backend makes calls to external URLs, it is configured to not follow redirects unless it is intended functionality.
Evidence or reason: The only server-side HTTP calls are to fixed vendor hosts (emailService.ts:136 api.resend.com, 155 api.sendgrid.com) plus SDK clients and OIDC discovery; no user-supplied URL is fetched (verified by grep). fetch() uses the default redirect: 'follow' (emailService.ts:136-153).
Gap: Redirect following is not configured, though all targets are fixed vendor hosts so exposure is low.
Fix: Pass redirect: 'error' to the vendor fetch calls and set the same on any future outbound fetch.

Requirement text: Verify that the application has countermeasures to protect against mass assignment attacks by limiting allowed fields per controller and action, e.g., it is not possible to insert or update a field value when it was not intended to be part of that action.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): User edit and booking edit allow-list fields; certificate edit by an owner limited to the file link. Tested by: tests/security/api.e2e.cjs. Original finding: Several update endpoints accept any column in the request body, allowing users to change fields they should never control (identity, retention flags, storage keys, booking status and cost), which can also be chained to read arbitrary stored files.
Gap: Provider, venue, course, session and policy routes and others still pass the body through.
Fix: Replace raw req.body with allowlisted zod schemas per action (self vs admin) on /api/users/:id, course-bookings, providers, venues, courses, sessions and policy matrix.

Requirement text: Verify that all proxying and middleware components transfer the user's original IP address correctly using trusted data fields that cannot be manipulated by the end user, and the application and web server use this correct value for logging and security decisions such as rate limiting, taking into account that even the original IP address may not be reliable due to dynamic IPs, VPNs, or corporate firewalls.
Evidence or reason: trust proxy is hard-coded to 1 hop (server/replitAuth.ts:102); the audit log takes the first X-Forwarded-For value from the client-controllable header (server/services/auditLog.ts:176) instead of req.ip; sign-in events record no IP at all (replitAuth.ts:153, auditLog.ts:127-131); no rate limiting or IP-based security decision exists. npm audit also reports a critical proxy-addr IP-spoofing advisory in the installed express chain.
Gap: The recorded source IP can be forged by any client, the proxy depth is not configurable for the company's WAF/load balancer chain, and sign-in records have no address.
Fix: Make trust proxy configurable (hop count/CIDR list), use req.ip everywhere, record IP on sign-in, and upgrade express/proxy-addr.

Requirement text: Verify that the application explicitly ensures that variables are of the correct type and performs strict equality and comparator operations. This is to avoid type juggling or type confusion vulnerabilities caused by the application code making an assumption about a variable type.
Evidence or reason: Strict equality is used throughout (no loose == or != comparisons found in server/*.ts apart from null checks); many routes validate with zod (about 120 parse/object calls in routes.ts) and newer routes check typeof on query values (routes.ts:3968, 4424, 4474, 5252). Counter-evidence: many handlers destructure req.body/req.query without type checks (routes.ts:405, 720, 871, 957, 1524, 2634, 3190, 8869, 8982) and cast with 'as string' (routes.ts:3206-3208, 7365).
Gap: Older endpoints trust the types of body and query values, so arrays or objects sent instead of strings can reach database calls or logic unchecked.
Fix: Add zod parsing (or typeof checks) at the top of the remaining handlers, starting with those listed, using one shared helper for query strings.

Requirement text: Verify that JavaScript code is written in a way that prevents prototype pollution, for example, by using Set() or Map() instead of object literals.
Evidence or reason: No explicit prototype-pollution defences: no Map/Object.create(null) use, no key allowlists (grep). Keys from uploaded files are used to build objects (routes.ts:597-599, trainingMatrixImport.ts, lifecycleImport.ts) and object spreads of req.body are used (routes.ts:1223). Counter-evidence: no recursive merge utilities are used in server code, and spread/assign of a '__proto__' JSON key does not pollute. The installed xlsx 0.18.5 has a known prototype-pollution advisory and parses uploaded files (routes.ts:579, 3575; services/lifecycleImport.ts:115; trainingMatrixImport.ts:93).
Gap: A known prototype-pollution library parses user-uploaded spreadsheets and file-derived keys are written to plain objects without guarding against __proto__ or constructor.
Fix: Replace xlsx, build header-keyed objects with Map or Object.create(null), and reject __proto__/constructor/prototype keys in imports.

Requirement text: Verify that the application has defenses against HTTP parameter pollution attacks, particularly if the application framework makes no distinction about the source of request parameters (query string, body parameters, cookies, or header fields).
Evidence or reason: Newer code checks typeof req.query.x === 'string' (routes.ts:3968, 4424, 4474, 4672, 5252; notificationRoutes.ts:35) which defeats repeated-parameter arrays; older routes take req.query values straight (routes.ts:720, 871, 907, 957, 971, 1762, 2161). Express default query parser turns repeated parameters into arrays; no HPP middleware exists.
Gap: Some endpoints pass repeated-parameter arrays into logic and filters unchecked.
Fix: Add a small query helper that coerces to a single string and apply it to the remaining routes.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that an inventory exists documenting the logging performed at each layer of the application's technology stack, what events are being logged, log formats, where that logging is stored, how it is used, how access to it is controlled, and for how long logs are kept.
Evidence or reason: No logging inventory exists. Actual logging: stdout/stderr text from console.* (server/vite.ts:11-20, index.ts:19-20,45-54), DB audit_events (server/services/auditLog.ts, migrations/0045_audit_events.sql), notification_logs with full email text (FOLLOW_UPS.md:57), sessions table. FOLLOW_UPS.md:114 notes no retention period for the audit log.
Gap: There is no document stating what is logged at each layer, formats, storage, access and retention.
Fix: Write the log inventory (app stdout, audit table, email log, platform/WAF/DB logs) with owners and retention.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that each log entry includes necessary metadata (such as when, where, who, what) that would allow for a detailed investigation of the timeline when an event happens.
Evidence or reason: Audit events carry who (actorId, name, role, acting-as), what (action, entity, field changes), when (occurred_at) and where (method, path, status, IP) (auditLog.ts:173-177, migration 0045 columns). Counter-evidence: sign-in events have no IP (replitAuth.ts:153, auditLog.ts:127-131); only successful changes are recorded (auditLog.ts:148); stdout lines have no actor, request id or full timestamp (vite.ts:11-20, index.ts:45).
Gap: Audit rows are well structured for successful changes, but failures and sign-ins lack metadata and the operational log has no actor or correlation id.
Fix: Add a request id, actor and source IP to stdout log lines and to sign-in and failure events.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that time sources for all logging components are synchronized, and that timestamps in security event metadata use UTC or include an explicit time zone offset. UTC is recommended to ensure consistency across distributed systems and to prevent confusion during daylight saving time transitions.
Evidence or reason: Audit export and API use ISO-8601 UTC (auditLog.ts:227, JSON Dates). Counter-evidence: stdout timestamp is local time with no date or zone (server/vite.ts:11-20); audit_events.occurred_at is 'timestamp' without time zone (migrations/0045_audit_events.sql:3) so UTC depends on server/DB timezone settings. Clock synchronisation is not an application matter.
Gap: Console log lines carry local time without zone and audit times rely on the host being set to UTC.
Fix: Log timestamps with new Date().toISOString(), use timestamptz for audit columns, run containers in UTC; platform to provide NTP.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that the application only stores or broadcasts logs to the files and services that are documented in the log inventory.
Evidence or reason: Without an inventory (V16.1.1) the destinations cannot be checked. Actual destinations: stdout/stderr, audit_events table, notification_logs table, audit CSV download (auditRoutes.ts:30-36). No file logging or third-party log shipping was found in server/ (grep).
Gap: Application writes only to stdout and its own database, which is consistent with a minimal inventory, but no inventory exists to confirm it, and the email log stores full message bodies.
Fix: Publish the inventory (V16.1.1) and add a retention limit on email bodies.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that logs can be read and correlated by the log processor that is in use, preferably by using a common logging format.
Evidence or reason: Audit events are structured rows with a jsonb 'changes' field (migration 0045). Operational logs are free-form text such as '9:58:31 AM [express] GET /api/auth/user 200 in 241ms :: {...' (server/vite.ts:19, index.ts:45-54) and multi-line console.error(error) dumps, which a log processor cannot parse reliably.
Gap: Application logs are unstructured and not machine-parsable; audit events are only in the database, not in the stream a log processor reads.
Fix: Emit one JSON line per request/event (timestamp, level, request id, actor, event) and also write audit events to stdout.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that when logging sensitive data, the application enforces logging based on the data's protection level. For example, it may not be allowed to log certain data, such as credentials or payment details. Other data, such as session tokens, may only be logged by being hashed or masked, either in full or partially.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): Response bodies are no longer written to the log. Tested by: by reading the code. Original finding: There is no protection-level rule for logging: response bodies, emails and database error details reach stdout, and personal field values are kept in audit changes.
Gap: Other log lines still include email addresses and database error text.
Fix: Delete the response-body capture from the request logger, log only ids, mask emails, and redact personal fields (dateOfBirth, companyNumber, vantageNumber) in audit changes.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that all authentication operations are logged, including successful and unsuccessful attempts. Additional metadata, such as the type of authentication or factors used, should also be collected.
Evidence or reason: Successful sign-ins are recorded (server/replitAuth.ts:153 -> services/auditLog.ts:127-131). Not logged: failed or abandoned sign-in (failureRedirect only, replitAuth.ts:181-186), token refresh failures (replitAuth.ts:240-243), sign-out (replitAuth.ts:188-197), the authentication type, or the source IP. The identity provider outside the app holds its own failure logs.
Gap: Only successful sign-ins are logged and they carry no IP or method; failures, refresh denials and logouts are invisible.
Fix: Log sign-in failure, refresh failure and sign-out with IP, user agent and outcome (use a custom callback in passport.authenticate), and obtain IdP logs.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that failed authorization attempts are logged. For L3, this must include logging all authorization decisions, including logging when sensitive data is accessed (without logging the sensitive data itself).
Evidence or reason: Authorisation denials return 403 without any log entry: requireRole (routes.ts:237-296), trainingPerm (297-306), checkCertificateOwnerOrRoles (308-356), direct 403s such as routes.ts:1186, 7393; the audit middleware skips non-2xx responses (auditLog.ts:148).
Gap: Failed authorisation attempts are not recorded anywhere, so probing and privilege abuse cannot be detected.
Fix: Log every 401/403 (actor, route, role, target id, IP) through the audit helper, rate-limited to avoid flooding.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that the application logs the security events that are defined in the documentation and also logs attempts to bypass the security controls, such as input validation, business logic, and anti-automation.
Evidence or reason: No security event definition exists, and attempts to bypass controls are not logged: input validation failures return 400 without logging (e.g. routes.ts:4526-4550 ZodError path), role denials not logged (V16.3.2), no anti-automation exists to log. Reads of personal records (CV, evidence, user records) are not logged (auditLog.ts:135 skips GET).
Gap: The application does not log validation bypass attempts, privilege denials, or access to sensitive records, and has no defined list of security events.
Fix: Define the security event list, log validation and authorisation failures and downloads of CVs/evidence/certificates, and alert on bursts.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that the application logs unexpected errors and security control failures such as backend TLS failures.
Evidence or reason: Unexpected errors are logged: global handler (server/index.ts:64-72), process-level handlers (index.ts:19-20), per-route console.error (about 420 sites in routes.ts), DB pool errors (server/db.ts:37), audit write failures (auditLog.ts:123,179). Counter-evidence: security-control failures are not logged (authorisation denials, V16.3.2), TLS failures to the database/SMTP are not specifically handled, and the process continues after uncaughtException (index.ts:20).
Gap: Generic errors are logged but security control failures and backend TLS failures are not recognised or surfaced.
Fix: Add explicit logging for control failures and for TLS/connect errors to DB, SMTP and the IdP; exit and restart on uncaughtException.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that all logging components appropriately encode data to prevent log injection.
Evidence or reason: Logs are plain text with raw interpolation of external values: console.log('...', req.params.id) (routes.ts:1065, a decoded path value so CR/LF can be injected), email addresses and ids (replitAuth.ts:77, storage.ts:1652,1781), error messages. The request logger uses JSON.stringify for the body fragment (index.ts:47) which does escape newlines, but nothing sanitises the rest. Audit summaries embed user-chosen names/labels (auditLog.ts:171) and the CSV export does not neutralise formula characters (auditLog.ts:214).
Gap: No log encoding or structured logging is used, so crafted values can forge log lines, and exported audit CSV can carry spreadsheet formulas.
Fix: Use a structured JSON logger that escapes control characters, and prefix =,+,-,@ with an apostrophe in CSV cells.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that logs are protected from unauthorized access and cannot be modified.
Evidence or reason: Audit log read access is limited to admin, super_admin and developer (server/auditRoutes.ts:11-15); the application exposes no edit or delete route for audit_events and states it is append-only (auditLog.ts:14). Counter-evidence: the app's own database role can update and delete rows, and does so in the anonymisation routine (retention.ts:107-110); no trigger, revoke, or hash chain exists (migration 0045); stdout logs are protected only by the platform.
Gap: Audit rows could be altered by anyone with database write access or by a compromised application, and the app itself rewrites them.
Fix: Revoke UPDATE/DELETE on audit_events from the runtime role (use a restricted role for anonymisation), add a tamper-evident hash chain or WORM export.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that logs are securely transmitted to a logically separate system for analysis, detection, alerting, and escalation. The aim is to ensure that if the application is breached, the logs are not compromised.
Evidence or reason: Operational logs go to stdout for the container platform to collect; audit events are stored only in the same application database (migrations/0045_audit_events.sql), not sent to a separate system. No log-forwarding code or configuration exists in the repo.
Gap: Audit events live in the application's own database and would be lost or alterable in a database compromise; the app does not forward them.
Fix: Also emit audit events as JSON on stdout so the platform ships them to the company SIEM, which must retain them separately with alerting.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that a generic message is returned to the consumer when an unexpected or security-sensitive error occurs, ensuring no exposure of sensitive internal system data such as stack traces, queries, secret keys, and tokens.
Evidence or reason: Changed 18 Nov 2026 (branch feature/security-hardening): The global handler and about 27 route handlers no longer send internal error text to the caller; failures on our side show a plain message and the detail goes to the log. Tested by: by reading the code. Original finding: Unexpected errors return internal error text to the caller, which can reveal storage keys, constraint names and data values.
Gap: Other handlers return validation detail on 4xx; to be reviewed.
Fix: Return a generic message and a correlation id for 5xx, log detail server-side only, and remove details: error.message from handlers.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that the application continues to operate securely when external resource access fails, for example, by using patterns such as circuit breakers or graceful degradation.
Evidence or reason: Some graceful degradation: DB pool idle-connection errors are caught (server/db.ts:37), email failures are caught per call and recorded (routes.ts:7273, 7556, 7639; FOLLOW_UPS.md:44), scheduled jobs catch their own errors (server/index.ts:130-163), object storage client is lazily created (objectStorage.ts:14-20). Counter-evidence: no timeouts or circuit breakers on any outbound call (emailService.ts:136,155; AI SDK calls); start-up awaits OIDC discovery (replitAuth.ts:142) so an IdP outage at boot stops the server from listening; AI routes return 500 with no fallback.
Gap: An unavailable or slow external service can hang requests or block start-up; there are no timeouts, retries or circuit breakers.
Fix: Add timeouts and AbortSignal to outbound calls, retry discovery in the background, and return a clear 503 when a dependency is down.

Chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
Requirement text: Verify that the application fails gracefully and securely, including when an exception occurs, preventing fail-open conditions such as processing a transaction despite errors resulting from validation logic.

Tested by: tests/security/auth.unit.ts. Original finding: The leaver block fails open on error and is skipped entirely on 79 routes, so a closed or expired session can still use them.
